articles.title: IDF soldier filmed shooting Palestinian in leg amid West Bank settler standoff
articles.summary:
Incident is latest to raise questions over Israel’s ability or willingness to stop violent settlers in occupied territory

An Israeli soldier shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg,…

blocks.text: An Israeli soldier shot a Palestinian man, wounding him in the leg, as settlers confronted villagers by grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land in the town of Faqqua in the occupied West Bank.

Eyewitnesses said that a group of settlers had entered the area with their livestock, prompting residents to try to stop them. Israeli forces then intervened and, according to men at the scene, opened fire at residents. One of them shot Qassem Hussam, a Palestinian man in his mid-30s, wounding him in the leg.
Reached by the Guardian, the IDF confirmed it had received a report of the incident and that the person who fired was one of its soldiers.

“Earlier today [Saturday], a report was received regarding friction between Israeli civilians and Palestinians near the area of Faqqua,” the IDF said. “An IDF force that was at the scene fired into the air and toward a Palestinian.”
Mohammed al-Sheikh, 34, who was standing next to Hussam, told the Guardian the confrontation began when villagers encountered Israeli settlers grazing livestock on Palestinian-owned land.

“Then the Israeli soldiers came,” al-Sheikh said. “They started shooting. One soldier shot Hussam and he fell to the ground. We immediately went to help him and move him away. We couldn’t get an ambulance to the area, so we took him to hospital in a private car.”
Hussam was taken to hospital in a light-to-moderate condition, according to the Palestine Red Crescent.

The Israeli military said the incident was being reviewed by commanders and that its findings would be forwarded to the relevant authorities for examination. The IDF added that the military was investigating the soldier who shot the Palestinian man, apparently in breach of army protocol, according to the Times of Israel.
Video of the incident shows a group of Israeli soldiers and settlers confronting unarmed Palestinian men before shots are fired.
The incident is the latest to raise questions over the Israeli government’s ability or willingness to curb violent settlers in the occupied West Bank, where attacks have continued to increase.

On 8 September, the UK prime minister, Andy Burnham, said he would “not stand by” as horrific suffering continued, writing in the Guardian that for too long the UK had been hesitant to act, “fearful of being accused of being anti-Israel”.

Ed Miliband, the UK’s foreign secretary, said the government would now take the official position that Israel’s occupation of the West Bank was unlawful in its entirety, and announced sweeping sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements.

The dramatic shift in the UK’s position came after a summer of intense diplomacy against a backdrop of rising settler violence in the West Bank, which led 12 countries, including France and Canada, to announce sanctions.

After Miliband described violent Jewish settler activity in the occupied West Bank as “ethnic cleansing” carried out with the tacit backing of the government of the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s foreign minister, Gideon Sa’ar, announced retaliatory measures including the closure of the consulate and entry bans on several MPs.
It marked the latest stage in a rapidly worsening dispute between the two countries, with diplomatic relations at their lowest point in years, even as violence in the West Bank has continued.

Israeli forces also carried out raids across Jenin governorate on Saturday, arresting six people and injuring a 14-year-old boy, who suffered a broken hand, according to the Palestinian news agency Wafa. Soldiers also raided several villages around Jenin, while forces entered at least five towns in Bethlehem governorate and set up a checkpoint at Za’atara.
East of Ramallah, Israeli settlers attacked the outskirts of Burqa, throwing stones at homes and vehicles.

On 4 September, two Palestinian teenagers were shot dead in al-Mughayyir after settlers entered the village under police and military escort and took dozens of sheep from a Palestinian home, residents and Israeli activists said.
The victims were Khalil Abu Alia, 16, and Omar al-Nassan, 19. Three other pupils from their 470-strong school had already been killed by Israeli soldiers and settlers this year.

According to the UN’s Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), more than 1,111 Palestinians, including at least 243 children, have been killed in the occupied West Bank, including East Jerusalem, since 7 October 2023.

articles.title: Bolick redeems self, Ahanmisi catches fire as Gilas Pilipinas rips Kazakhstan in Asian Games
articles.summary: Robert Bolick and Jerrick Ahanmisi spearhead Gilas Pilipinas' scoring spree from three-point range as the defending champions earn their first win in the Asian Games and boost their chances of…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Robert Bolick rebounded from a scoreless outing, while Jerrick Ahanmisi shot the lights out as Gilas Pilipinas claimed its first win in the Asian Games, dealing Kazakhstan a 109-78 beating at the Aichi International Arena in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday, September 12.

Held scoreless in a narrow 89-85 loss to Bahrain the day prior, Bolick fired 20 points in just a little over 15 minutes to help the defending champion Philippines improve to an even 1-1 record in Group C and boost its chances of advancing to the quarterfinals.

Ahanmisi, meanwhile, erupted for a game-high 22 points on a 7-of-11 clip from beyond the arc, torching the Kazakhs in a fourth-quarter scoring spree that allowed the Filipinos to break the game wide open.
Gilas Pilipinas held a slim 18-15 lead at the end of the opening period before Bolick took charge and scattered 13 points in the second frame as it mounted a 50-37 halftime advantage.

Ahanmisi then picked up where Bolick left off, knocking down five three-pointers in the fourth quarter and singlehandedly outscoring the entire Kazakhstan team, which managed just 12 points in the final period of the 31-point blowout.

Calvin Oftana, who erupted for 31 points in the loss to the Bahrainis, still made his presence felt with 12 points, while Sedrick Barefield contributed 11 points, 5 assists, and 4 rebounds as he redeemed himself after going scoreless last game.
Zavier Lucero also delivered a near double-double outing of 10 points and 9 rebounds in the win, which saw the Filipinos sink 16 of their 29 attempts from long range for a healthy 55% shooting.
Bolick and Barefield, who both went 0-of-5 from three-point land against Bahrain, made 4 and 3 triples, respectively, this time around.

One of the few bright spots last game before he tweaked his right ankle late in the fourth quarter, Adrian Nocum played just a little under 16 minutes against the Kazakhs, contributing 4 points and 3 assists.
Anton Bykov produced 15 points and 10 rebounds to show the way for Kazakhstan, which fell to 0-2 after also absorbing a 38-point drubbing from China.
Given a one-day break, the Philippines turns its attention to unbeaten China in its last game of the group stage on Monday, September 14, with a win sending the Filipinos to the quarterfinals.
Only the top two teams from each of the three groups and the two best third-place teams will reach the knockout rounds.
Philippines 109 – Ahanmisi 22, Bolick 20, Oftana 12, Barefield 11, Lucero 10, Baltazar 6, Arana 6, Abarrientos 6, Trollano 5, Nocum 4, Ganuelas-Rosser 4, Bates 3.
Kazakhstan 78 – Bykov 15, Marat 12, Maydekin 12, Neff 11, Rabchenyuk 9, Murzagaliyev 8, Fedchenko 7, Ivanov 2, Sakhipov 2, Severgin 0, Marchuk 0, Kuanov 0.

articles.title: Nashville airport board unanimously approves name change to honor Dolly Parton
articles.summary:
The city’s mayor and Tennessee’s governor threw their support behind the name change last month

The Nashville airport is to be…

blocks.text: The Nashville airport is to be renamed after Dolly Parton, a board of commissioners voted on Friday, in tribute to the Smoky Mountain singer who is estimated to bring $1.8bn each year to Tennessee through her Dollywood theme park.
The decision ensures that Parton, who died last month at 80 years old, will be memorialized with her name on an airport, although the renaming process will take time to complete.
In her lifetime, Parton did not think the idea, which came about last year, would come to fruition.
“I think that’s probably more of a joke than anything,” Parton told the Tennessean. “I mean, it does sound like a lot of fun to say: ‘Your flight is departin’ from Nashville’s D Parton.’”
The move to rename gained traction last month when the Nashville mayor, Freddie O’Connell, and the Tennessee governor, Bill Lee, threw their support behind the name change.
“Dolly Parton’s extraordinary life is forever woven into the fabric of our state,” Lee said in a statement, recognizing what he called her “Volunteer spirit”.

“It is fitting that Nashville international airport would bear the name of our state’s favorite daughter and greet travelers with the enduring legacy of Dolly’s music, generosity, faith and kindness,” Lee added.
After the airport’s commissioners voted in favor of the change, Lee said it was an “important step to honor her remarkable legacy” as “Dolly has always helped the world fall in love with Tennessee”.

The name change is likely to be pricey since it will require new signage across the entire 4,500-acre (1,700-hectare) property, and updates to an airport monuments, merchandise, shuttle buses, uniforms, business cards, legal contracts and leases.

Although the new airport name in her honor has not been decided, Tennessean columnist Alejandro Ramos argued last month that the case for the change “is larger than music” because of her contributions to the state of Tennessee and to international literacy through her Imagination Library charity.

“Parton’s songs helped make Tennessee recognizable around the world. But her deepest legacy may be what she did with the success that followed. She accumulated the kind of fame, wealth and influence few people ever experience. Then she repeatedly turned those resources outward,” Ramos wrote.

The Metropolitan Nashville Airport Authority said in a statement: “While a final name has not yet been determined, we are working closely with the appropriate parties to thoughtfully determine how Dolly Parton’s name and legacy will be incorporated”.

articles.title: Marcos taps Indian rail firm for Mindanao, Cebu, PNR projects
articles.summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. met with an Indian railway company on Saturday to explore studies for three proposed railway systems in the Philippines, including projects in Mindanao and…

blocks.text: Published September 12, 2026 9:28pm

President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. met with an Indian railway company on Saturday to explore studies for three proposed railway systems in the Philippines, including projects in Mindanao and Cebu and the extension of the Philippine National Railways (PNR) from Tutuban in Manila.
The meeting took place during the 8th BRICS Summit in India.

BRICS is an association of developing economies, of which the Philippines is not a member. Marcos said in his departure message that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi invited him to attend the summit as the 2026 ASEAN chair and as an outreach participant, or a non-member country invited to join the summit discussions.
In a “24 Oras Weekend” report by Darlene Cay, Marcos arrived in India at 11:15 p.m. New Delhi time.
Marcos said he would advocate for global governance, disaster preparedness and international cooperation during the summit.

“We will call for fairer global governance, stronger disaster preparedness, and responsible use of new technologies, climate action and the peaceful settlement of disputes under international law,” Marcos said.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin also attended the BRICS Summit. However, the Department of Foreign Affairs said Marcos would not hold formal dialogues with either leader.
Marcos said he wanted to ensure that the Philippines remained open to engaging with various countries while upholding international law and responsible conduct in maritime areas.
“We must now ensure that the sea lanes are just as free, open, and governed by law, rules, and responsible behavior,” Marcos said.

The President also met with representatives of the Indian Space Research Organisation and the Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure, which shared insights on disaster management and resilience.

“The meeting was about the experiences of coalition members in dealing with disasters and how to become more disaster-resilient. At the same time, they will also help us access financing,” Presidential Communications Office Secretary Dave Gomez said.

According to Cay’s report, Marcos was also scheduled to meet with Modi to assess the progress of the five-year plan of action between the Philippines and India. It would be their first meeting since Marcos’ state visit to India last year.

“Our discussions will cover defense and maritime cooperation, trade and investment, the proposed preferential trade agreement, health and pharmaceuticals, digital cooperation, tourism, direct air connectivity, and people-to-people ties,” Marcos said.
“It will also be an auspicious occasion to renew our invitation for Prime Minister Modi to visit Manila for the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit in November,” he added.
Marcos was scheduled to attend the BRICS Gala Dinner on the evening of September 12 and deliver a speech during the opening session on September 13.— Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Senate impeachment court: 11 votes to overturn 16-vote threshold
articles.summary: To convict Vice President Sara Duterte, senator-judges need 11 votes to overturn the 16-vote threshold, Senate impeachment court spokesperson Atty. Reginald Tongol clarified on Saturday.... Keep on…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — To convict Vice President Sara Duterte, senator-judges need 11 votes to overturn the 16-vote threshold, Senate impeachment court spokesperson Atty. Reginald Tongol clarified on Saturday.
His clarificatory remarks followed his earlier statement on Friday that a majority of 10 votes would be needed to change the threshold amid the absence of some senator-judges due to legal issues.
The impeachment court is set to revisit the voting threshold on Wednesday, September 16 before the prosecution and defense present their arguments on September 23.
He added that according to the Office of the Clerk of Court, the impeachment court’s presiding officer, Sen. Francis Escudero may also vote to change the 16-vote ruling to convict Duterte.
“So, kunwari po, 20 po o yung umattend po, so kailangan po hindi 10, kundi 11 po para po ma-overturn po yung ruling,” he said..
(If 20 senators are present, not, 10, but 11 votes re needed to overturn the ruling.)

“So kahapon po nung sinabi ko po yun, ina-apply lamang po yung pagkakaalam po ukol sa parliamentary rules kasi nakalagay po sa Rule 41, Section 116 po ng rules ng Senado na supplementarily applicable katulad na nakalagay sa Rule 6 ng Senate Impeachment Rules na hindi po boboto ang president on the matter unless his vote is decisive,” he explained during a DWIZ interview.

(So, when I stated that yesterday, I was simply applying the principles of parliamentary rules, specifically Rule 41, Section 116 of the Senate Rules, which is supplementarily applicable alongside Rule 6 of the Senate Impeachment Rules— stipulating that the President shall not vote on the matter unless his vote is decisive.”)
Supreme Court review
Tongol said that there is still a possibility that the matter would be assessed by the Supreme Court if ever a party raises a concern or a petition against overturning the 16-vote threshold.

“Kung ngayon po magkaroon ng desisyon yung Senado to overturn his appeal, any party naman po pwedeng umakyat sa Korte Suprema to question it for grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction,” he said.

(If the Senate were to decide today to overturn his appeal, any party could elevate the matter to the Supreme Court to challenge it on the grounds of grave abuse of discretion amounting to lack or excess of jurisdiction.)

The Senate impeachment court on Thursday appointed three Supreme Court chief justices and one retired associate justice as amici curiae, or ‘friends of the court’, to provide legal assistance on the issue.
Tongol assured that impeachment proceedings would continue even if a petition for certiorari would be filed before the higher court.

“Kasi nakalagay po sa Rule 65, na kahit po merong petition for certiorari sa Korte Suprema, ay magpapatuloy pa rin po ang proceedings doon sa lower court na kung saan na walang TRO (Temporary Restraining Order) na inissue,” he explained.

(“Because Rule 65 states that even if there is a petition for certiorari before the Supreme Court, the proceedings in the lower court will continue if no Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) has been issued.”)
He further said that “only when there is a TRO issued, don lamang hindi magpapatuloy ang proseso,”
(Only when there is a TRO issued can the process be halted.)

articles.title: Donald Trump says he would ‘love’ to see united Ireland
articles.summary:
US president say on visit to republic that unification will happen eventually so ‘may as well happen now’

•

blocks.text: Donald Trump has said he would “love” to see a united Ireland and that it “may as well happen now”.

The US president appeared to endorse the push for constitutional change on the island at the start of a two-day visit to Ireland on Saturday. The unexpected intervention prompted a swift rebuttal from the UK government and Northern Ireland’s unionist leaders.

“I don’t want ⁠to cause any problems, ​but ‌I will ‌tell you, I’d love ‌to see it unified,” Trump told reporters at joint press conference with the taoiseach, Micheál Martin, in Dublin. “I think it would be a great feather in everybody’s cap if that happened. You know what? The way I look at it, it’s going to happen eventually. It may as well happen now.”

The unification of Northern Ireland with the republic of Ireland would be “fantastic”, Trump said. “The UK will have something to say about it, obviously. But I think it would be a great thing. I mean, how can it be bad?”

blocks.caption: Micheál Martin welcomes Donald Trump to Farmleigh House, in Dublin, during his trip to the Republic of Ireland. Photograph: Ben Birchall/PA

blocks.text: The intervention jolted his hosts and came two weeks after Andy Burnham said a referendum on unification was “off the table”, which angered Sinn Féin and other Irish nationalists.

Speaking later on Saturday, Trump acknowledged that his comments on unification, made in response to a reporter’s question, would be controversial. “No matter what you say or how you say it, there’s no good answer,” he said. “I gave a nice answer, I think. We’ll worry about it tomorrow.” Unification, he added, would be a “very cool thing”.
A Downing Street spokesperson said the prime minister still believed there was not the required support for unification to trigger a referendum, as set out in the Good Friday agreement.
Gavin Robinson, the Democratic Unionist party (DUP) leader, said Northern Ireland’s constitutional future would be decided by its people, not by commentary in London, Dublin or Washington.

“Northern Ireland is part of the United Kingdom because that is the settled democratic will of its people. I am confident Northern Ireland will continue to choose the UK and the security it offers. As unionists we are not interested in the destruction of our country by joining with the Irish republic.”

Colum Eastwood, an MP and former leader of the Social Democratic and Labour party (SDLP), and frequent critic of Trump, posted a clip of the president’s remarks on social media and wrote: “Always liked him.”

The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, said: “President Trump is shooting from the hip as usual, just like he did with Greenland and Canada becoming the 51st state. This sort of loose talk about the future of democratic countries is deeply unhelpful and creates unnecessary tension.”

blocks.caption: Demonstrators protesting against Trump’s visit in Dublin. Photograph: Natalia Campos/Reuters

blocks.text: Trump’s comments strayed from predecessors who sought to keep the White House neutral on Ireland’s constitutional future, but the off-the-cuff nature of the remarks suggested there was no change in US policy.

Trump’s unofficial visit is centred on golf – he flew on Saturday afternoon to his resort in Doonbeg, County Clare, which is hosting the Irish Open – but started with a courtesy call in Dublin to Áras an Uachtaráin, the official residence and workplace of the Irish president, Catherine Connolly.

Before her election to the ceremonial post last year, Connolly called Trump a bully and criticised his policies in Gaza and Iran. Their brief encounter, behind closed doors, appeared to go smoothly despite a coded critique of White House policies.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Donald Trump and Catherine Connolly at her presidential residence in Phoenix Park, Dublin. Photograph: Tony Maxwell/PA

blocks.text: Connolly said in a statement afterwards that she “conveyed the strong view of the Irish people that the normalisation of war and genocide can never be accepted” and stressed the importance of the United Nations – an organisation Trump has disparaged. Trump said they had a wide-ranging discussion, including about energy and water, and that Connolly was “terrific”.

Trump held a separate meeting with Martin at the Phoenix Park, where he told the press that Iran would seek peace after the US midterm elections and repeated his claim that his war had prevented Tehran obtaining a nuclear weapon.
Asked about protests against his visit – a large crowd was expected in central Dublin, 5 miles away, as well as at Doonbeg – the president said he had not seen any protests.

blocks.caption: Spectators watch as Air Force One flies Trump over the Irish Open in Doonbeg, County Clare. Photograph: Damien Eagers/PA

blocks.text: Addressing guests as at the US ambassador’s residence, Trump assailed US Democrats as extremists and criticised Europe’s approach to immigration.

He lauded US-Irish relations but reiterated a complaint about the American pharma giants in Ireland. “You took all our medical companies, we’ve got to get a couple of them back. You fleeced us but that’s OK. There’s a lot of room to go around and our relationship with you is fantastic.”
As he left Dublin a crowd at the Garden of Remembrance waved banners and chanted: “Donald Trump, can you hear? We don’t want you here.”
Trump is expected to stay overnight in Doonbeg and present the Irish Open trophy before returning to Washington on Sunday.

articles.title: 10 senators can overturn 16-vote threshold to convict Sara Duterte - Tongol
articles.summary: At least 10 senators can overturn the ruling of Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero that 16 votes are needed to remove Vice President Sara Duterte from office, court…

blocks.text: At least 10 senators can overturn the ruling of Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis Escudero that 16 votes are needed to remove Vice President Sara Duterte from office, court spokesperson Regie Tongol said Friday.

Of the 24 senators, four are currently absent, while Escudero would not participate, leaving 19 senators to decide on the matter on September 23, Tongol told reporters. Under a simple majority vote, he said, this means only 10 senators would be needed to overturn the 16-vote threshold for conviction.
“Majority of the quorum present po ang makakaboto. Parang ordinary action lamang po ito ng Senado,” Tongol said.
(The votes of the majority of the quorum present will be the basis. This is just like an ordinary action of the Senate.)

Currently, Senators Jinggoy Estrada and Rodante Marcoleta are detained over separate plunder charges, while Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa is in hiding amid an arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court (ICC) in connection with the Duterte administration’s war on drugs.
Senator Loren Legarda has not attended the trial for several weeks as she remains abroad on extended medical leave.
However, Tongol said that there is still a possibility that more than the expected 20 senator-judges could be present on voting day.
He also said that in the event of a tie among the senator-judges, the motion on the voting threshold would be considered to have “failed.”
“So the ruling of the presiding officer will stand,” he said.
Speaking to reporters on Friday, Duterte said it had already been decided that the 1987 Constitution would be followed in determining the threshold for conviction.
“So ibig sabihin, ngayon na nagbago 'yung usapan, ibig sabihin ay babaguhin nila. Bakit pa ba natin pag-uusapan 'yun kung hindi naman babaguhin, 'di ba?” she added.
(So that means, now the conversation has changed, it means they will change it. Why are we even talking about it if it’s not going to be changed, right?)
Her brother, Davao City Representative Paolo “Pulong” Duterte, said 10 votes cannot override the Constitution.
"Ten votes to reverse the 16-vote rule? Are you sure about this? Ten votes to change the Constitution? Di puwede (That is not allowed)," he wrote on Facebook on Saturday.

"Ang Constitution mismo ang nagsasabi ng 'two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.' Kung ang bilang ng senators ngayon ay 24, that translates to 16 kasi 'all' ang sabi ng Constitution. Para sa mga law benders natin, baka di niyo alam ang ibig sabihin ng 'all.' Wala yang karugtung na 'all present' or 'all law benders.'"

(The Constitution itself says ‘two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.’ If there are currently 24 senators, that translates to 16 because the Constitution says ‘all.’ For our law benders, perhaps you don’t know what ‘all’ means. There is no qualifier after ‘all’ saying ‘all present’ or ‘all law benders.’")

At the start of the impeachment trial on July 6, Escudero said that under Article XI, Section 3, Paragraph 6 of the 1987 Constitution, no person shall be convicted without the concurrence of two-thirds of all the members of the Senate.
With the Senate composed of 24 members, Escudero said a literal interpretation of the constitutional provision means a conviction requires at least 16 affirmative votes.
Senator Erwin Tulfo made a manifestation during the September 8 hearing, seeking clarification on the 16-vote threshold, given that four senator-judges are currently not attending the trial.
Tulfo also said it must be clarified whether senators who are detained will be allowed to vote or whether their votes will be accepted by the court even if they are not attending the trial.

To settle the matter, Escudero said the court invited four amici curiae (friends of the court)—retired Supreme Court Chief Justices Hilario Davide, Artemio Panganiban, and Reynato Puno, and former SC Justice Adolf Azcuna—to weigh in on the voting threshold on September 16.
The oral arguments between the defense and prosecution panels, meanwhile, will be held on September 23, with each side given 15 minutes to present its position.
After the oral arguments, the senator-judges are expected to cast their votes. —VBL, GMA News

articles.title: Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger
articles.summary: Winemakers can make bubbly up to up to 15% ABV following an unusual harvest that produced sweeter grapes.

blocks.text: The temporary increase in champagne's alcohol content is only expected to affect a small number of wines, a spokeswoman for the Comite Champagne told the BBC.

During the second fermentation process, which gives champagne its bubbles, "a very small number of wines from this harvest could have slightly exceeded the regulatory limit of 13%, reaching around 13.1% or 13.2%".
"Therefore a decision was made to exceptionally and temporarily increase the regulatory limit to 15% - only for this year," she said.
The first grapes were cut in early August and the harvest expanded by the middle of the month, "the earliest ever recorded in Champagne", the association said.

"The 2026 growing season will be remembered as one of the most unusual in Champagne's history, marked by severe spring frosts of historic intensity, an exceptionally early flowering period and five heatwaves throughout the summer." it added.

Speaking in the Times newspaper, Stéphane Vignon, a producer in Verzenay said: "The Mediterranean climate is moving north. This is year one of a new cycle. It's unlikely to be every year, but it will happen again".
Higher-strength champagne is unlikely to be an obvious selling point, warned Jane Anson, a wine columnist and author based in Bordeaux.
She told the Times: "Today people increasingly prefer lower-alcohol
"The battle between what consumers want and what nature provides must be very stressful for producers."
The 2026 vintage is unlikely to hit shelves until 2028 as champagne must age for at least 15 months.

articles.title: PGH specialists examining Romualdez after hospital transfer
articles.summary: Following former House Speaker Martin Romualdez' transfer from Cardinal Santos Medical Center, the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) on Saturday said it formed a team of specialists to conduct an…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines—Following former House Speaker Martin Romualdez’ transfer from Cardinal Santos Medical Center, the Philippine General Hospital (PGH) on Saturday said it formed a team of specialists to conduct an examination on him.

PGH, in In a statement, said the team of doctors will conduct the needed medical examinations and diagnostic tests on the former speaker before submitting a comprehensive report to the Sandiganbayan by Sunday afternoon.
The hospital said: “Ito ang magiging batayan ng rekomendasyon ng PGH kung kinakailangan ang patuloy na pananatili ni Congressman Romualdez sa ospital.”
(This will be the basis of the PGH’s recommendation if the continued confinement of Congressman Romualdez in the hospital is necessary.)
The PGH assured that it will remain objective and professional in conducting its examination.
Confidentiality
It added that no medical information regarding Romualdez’s condition will be released, except for the report that will be submitted before the court, to protect the patient’s confidentiality.
The Sandiganbayan Third Division on Friday ordered the transfer of Romualdez from Cardinal Santos Medical Center to PGH in order to conduct an independent examination on the former speaker.
Romualdez had filed a manifestation requesting for his continued hospital confinement, after he was arrested at Cardinal Santos on Monday over charges of plunder.

articles.title: Iraq scrambles to address fallout from alleged militia attack on Saudi oil pipeline
articles.summary: Iraq’s government was racing Saturday to contain the fallout after local Iran-backed militias were accused of attacking and shuttering a key Saudi pipeline.

image.caption: Fighters loyal to the Houthi authorities shout slogans during a rally to recruit more fighters, in Sanaa, Yemen's capital, on Thursday. The country relapsed into war in July after years of calm, drawn into the regional conflict triggered by the U.S.-Israeli offensive against Iran that began Feb. 28.

blocks.text: World·New
Iraq’s government was racing Saturday to contain the fallout after local Iran-backed militias were accused of attacking and shuttering a key Saudi pipeline.
Iran-backed militias deny involvement in strike
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Sep 12, 2026 8:40 AM EDT | Last Updated: 20 minutes ago
Iraq's government was racing Saturday to contain the fallout after local Iran-backed militias were accused of attacking and shuttering a key Saudi pipeline.

Though an umbrella group of Iran-backed militias in Iraq denied their involvement, Iraq's government confirmed the attacks had originated from its territory. The government pledged to investigate and dismissed a military commander.

The country is under mounting pressure to prevent local militias from aiding other Iran proxy groups across the region. The Iraqi government has set a Sept. 30 deadline for non-state groups to disarm, but several of the most powerful militias have said they will not comply.

Pressure to disarm the militias is especially acute as the Iran-backed Houthi rebels make an advance across Yemen’s west coast in a major setback to the Saudi-backed coalition that risks escalating the war in the region. The Houthis on Friday seized an island in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key shipping lane through which about 12 per cent of global trade passes.

Their virtual control of the strait could send global oil prices — already inflated by the six-month Iran-U.S. war — spiralling. The strait has become a vital commercial lane for Saudi oil ever since the Iran war disrupted shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

items: Houthis seize strategic island, Saudis close pipeline as fighting escalates

blocks.text: Asked about the region on Saturday while speaking to reporters in Dublin, U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran was "probably" responsible for the pipeline attack but tried to calm concerns.
He said his administration has "had discussions" with the Houthis, though he did not specify to which talks he was referring.
"The Houthis called us, and they don't want to fight with us," Trump said. "They would much prefer not having us involved, and they're letting most ships go through."
Iraq to investigate attack on Saudi pipeline

A group of Iran-backed militias in Iraq denied in a statement on Saturday that they were responsible for the attacks on the East-West crude oil pipeline in Saudi Arabia, while praising the Houthis for their "ongoing battlefield victories against Saudi forces."
The group said it would co-operate with the Iraqi government's investigation.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi said earlier Saturday that he'd ordered an investigation into the operations command of Maysan province, along the border with Iran, and dismissed the province's commander.

Saudi Arabia shut down the major, cross-country oil pipeline on Friday, calling it a "precautionary measure" after the pipeline came under drone attack. It blamed the attacks on several drones that came from Iraq but said the kingdom would not retaliate, to give the Iraqi government "an opportunity to take the necessary measures."
Several Arab countries, including Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Egypt, condemned the attack on Saturday, according to the Saudi state news agency.

items: Iran-backed Houthis attack Saudi oil facilities, injuring dozens

blocks.text: Built in the 1980s, the East-West pipeline has played an important role in Saudi Arabia's ability to export oil following the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war. By early June, Saudi Arabia had more than doubled oil exports from the Red Sea port at the pipeline's end to more than five million barrels per day, according to the International Energy Agency.

Tehran-backed Iraqi militias have carried out strikes on U.S.-linked targets both inside and outside of Iraq since the U.S. and Israel attacked Iran on Feb. 28, and have co-ordinated with Yemen's Houthi rebels to attack Saudi Arabia.
Iraq closes border crossings with Iran
In a move possibly linked to the investigation, Iraq closed two key border crossings with Iran, Iraq's state-run news agency reported Saturday.
The report said that Iraqi officials were at the border, investigating previous "violations and infractions" at the crossings.

Valiollah Hayati, the deputy governor of Iran's southwestern Khuzestan province, named the closed crossings as Shalamcheh and Chazabeh. They are among the main official border crossings between Iran and Iraq.
Iranian state media said the measure would halt all passenger and commercial traffic through the two crossings until further notice.

Saudi Arabia and the United States bombed Iranian-backed militias in Iraq in July after blaming them for drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities that had been claimed by the Houthis. Regional officials told The Associated Press that the Houthis helped the Iraqi militias plan and execute the attacks.
Fighting threatens to reignite Yemen’s civil war

The escalating fighting threatens to end a fragile truce that had largely halted Yemen's civil war since 2022. At stake are 40 million people in the Arab world's poorest country. The conflict killed 150,000 and brought many others to the brink of famine.
The surge in fighting in the past week has sent more than 46,000 people fleeing, the United Nations migration agency said Friday.

The Houthis have been at war with Yemen's government since 2014, when the rebels seized much of northern and central Yemen and the capital, Sanaa. Saudi Arabia entered the war the following year on the side of the government.

articles.title: Calls for Democrats to be shot go unchallenged at Republican convention
articles.summary:
Crowd member repeatedly said some Democrats ‘should be shot’ during Ted Cruz’s speech, without senator responding

On the night Republicans gathered to mourn the killing of Charlie Kirk and…

blocks.text: On the night Republicans gathered to mourn the killing of Charlie Kirk and warn against the dangers of violent rhetoric, a crowd at the party’s irregular midterm convention in Dallas repeatedly called for a sitting Senate candidate to be shot, while the Republican senator at the podium never denounced or even noted the outbursts.

The outbursts came repeatedly during Ted Cruz’s Thursday night address at the American Airlines center, when he named a Democrat he accused of holding radical views. After the senator mentioned the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, video footage depicts at least one audience member shouting: “He should be shot!” The same cry followed when Cruz named Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and again after he named Texas Senate candidate James Talarico. Cruz did not pause or respond to the shouting, and it remains unclear whether he heard it from the stage. Cruz did not respond to a request for comment.

Cruz had accused Mamdani of wanting to seize the means of production, said El-Sayed felt an “obligation” to follow Sharia law and claimed Talarico wanted to dismantle capitalism. Each characterization stretched past remarks the three men had actually made in other contexts.

Asked about the moment on CNN’s The Source With Kaitlan Collins, El-Sayed said such rhetoric had become dangerously normalized and that it should unsettle anyone who heard it. He called on Republicans to name the chant for what it was: incitement that both parties ought to reject, and appealed for a return to a politics centered on people’s basic needs and dignity.

“Look, I’m a dad with two daughters, and I hope those daughters get to grow up and live with their dad. This is what has become the norm in our politics … literally calls to violence and the inability for anybody to actually call it out,” El-Sayed said.
“We can learn to disagree agreeably, and when you hear that kind of call to violence, it should be shuddering to all of us,” he added.

A spokesperson for Mike Rogers, the Republican former congressman challenging El-Sayed for Michigan’s open Senate seat who was in Dallas for the convention, said Rogers condemned the remarks and “all political violence”.

The convention fell on the first anniversary of the assassination of conservative commentator Charlie Kirk, an occasion Republican speakers repeatedly invoked, including the vice-president, JD Vance, who spoke of his friendship with Kirk during a headlining address.

El-Sayed is locked in one of the cycle’s most closely watched Senate races. A CNN poll released on Wednesday showed him leading Rogers 47% to 44% in the contest to succeed the retiring Democratic senator Gary Peters, as both parties fight for control of the chamber.

articles.title: Gilas routs Kazakhstan, stays alive in Asian Games quarterfinals race
articles.summary: LIVE: Gilas Pilipinas vs Kazakhstan – Asian Games 2026 men’s basketball MANILA, Philippines–Gilas Pilipinas kept its quarterfinal hopes alive in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 men’s basketball…

blocks.text: FILE – Robert Bolick with a breakout game for Gilas Pilipinas in a game against Kazakhstan in the Asian Games 2026 men’s basketball. –FIBA
LIVE: Gilas Pilipinas vs Kazakhstan – Asian Games 2026 men’s basketball
MANILA, Philippines–Gilas Pilipinas kept its quarterfinal hopes alive in the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 men’s basketball 5-on-5 event after blowing out Kazakhstan, 109-78, on Saturday.
Robert Bolick finally delivered a big performance while a barrage of threes in the fourth quarter enabled Gilas to slam the door shut on Kazakhstan and barge into the win column in Group C.

Jerrick Ahanmisi sizzled for seven three-pointers on his way to 22 points while Bolick scored 13 of his 20 points despite being a game-time decision with a knee injury and struggling since the two-game exhibition series with South Korea in Suwon the previous weekend.

blocks.caption: Gilas Pilipinas men's Jerrick Ahanmisi during a game in the Fiba 3x3 Asia Cup.

blocks.text: FILE–Gilas Pilipinas men’s Jerrick Ahanmisi. –FIBA 3×3
The Philippines improved to 1-1, bouncing back from a 69-65 loss to Bahrain the previous day in a rough start to its quest to defend the gold it won three years ago in Hangzhou, China.
Bahrain was beaten, 105-59, by China earlier in the day, giving the Chinese side a 2-0 slate and the group lead.
Gilas also gained an inside track in the race for two of the three best third-place slots, tying Iran of Group B while ahead of Group A’s Saudi Arabia, which has a 0-2 slate.
Next up for Gilas is China, with plenty of implications for its chances of getting out of the group stage.
Three other players scored in double figures for Gilas in Calvin Oftana, Sedrick Barefield and Zavier Lucero.
Oftana had a modest 12-point output after going off for 31 against Bahrain, Barefield had 11 points on top of four rebounds and five assists while Lucero added 10 points and nine rebounds.

articles.title: Trained cops to replace 86 no-show teachers for Barmm poll duties
articles.summary: COTABATO CITY – Eighty six teachers tasked to serve during the first Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary elections on Monday have not reported during the final testing…

blocks.text: COTABATO CITY – Eighty six teachers tasked to serve during the first Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao parliamentary elections on Monday have not reported during the final testing and sealing of Automated Counting Machines (ACMs) were replaced by police personnel, Commission on Elections (Comelec) Chairman George Erwin Garcia said.

Speaking during the meeting with Asian Network for Free Elections (Anfrel) and National Democractic Institute (NDI) at the Comelec command center here, Garcia said the teachers were replaced by members of Special Electoral Board who are police officers trained for election duties.
Gardia said the police officers were duly trained and certified by the Department of Science and Technology to operate the ACMs.

“They (teachers) did not show up during the testing and sealing of ACMs and our protocol is they will be replaced by special electoral board,” Garcia said, adding that there was no official information why the 86 public school teachers did not show up.
Garcia also announced that all the electoral boards across the region have done the testing and sealing which means 100 percent ACMs to be used on Monday have been tested and sealed.
“All the election paraphernalia, except the ballots, are already in the hands of electoral boards,” Garcia said.
“The ballots, the number one accountable forms, would be picked up at past 12 a.m. on the 14th of September.”

articles.title: Deadly Russian strikes hit Ukraine after Putin's warning to European leaders
articles.summary: Russian strikes killed three civilians and wounded dozens in Ukraine, local officials said Saturday, after Russian President Vladimir Putin warned that sending European troops into Ukraine would…

image.caption: Firefighters work at the site of a gas station that was destroyed after being hit by a Russian drone strike, in Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, on Friday. (Alina Smutko/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

Russian strikes killed three civilians and wounded dozens in Ukraine, local officials said Saturday, after Russian President Vladimir Putin warned that sending European troops into Ukraine would amount to direct conflict with Russia.
3 killed and dozens wounded in Russian offensive
· The Associated Press
· Posted: Sep 12, 2026 8:16 AM EDT | Last Updated: 9 minutes ago

Ukraine is under mounting pressure from Russia’s intensifying air campaign that uses ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones to pierce defences. Moscow’s attacks have targeted Ukraine’s power grid ahead of winter in what officials say is meant to demoralize civilians.
Two people were killed and one wounded when Russian drones struck a residential area overnight in the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, regional head Ivan Fedorov said Saturday.
One person died and three others were wounded in strikes on Kryvyi Rih, according to local officials.

In the Black Sea port of Odesa and the surrounding area, 35 people were wounded in what regional head Oleh Kiper called a "massive attack." Among the buildings hit was a residential highrise, whose upper floors were completely destroyed.

items: Zelenskyy describes Canada-U.S. tensions as 'strange,' draws comparison to Ukraine and Russia

blocks.text: Putin, speaking to reporters at the BRICS summit in India on Friday, said that if European governments send troops into Ukraine, it will mean "a war with Russia."
"Now they’re talking about how they’re considering sending troops into Ukraine. That means a war with Russia," he said.
Some European leaders have pledged their commitment to a potential peacekeeping force, a prospect that Moscow has repeatedly described as unacceptable.
Putin denies threat to Europe, despite incursions
Putin also denied Russia posed any threat to Europe, saying "there is no such threat and never has been."
"We do not threaten, nor do we intend to threaten, European countries," he said.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said Thursday that two incidents along Ukraine’s borders with Poland and Moldova this week were a preview of potential intensified Russian provocations at Ukraine’s border crossing points with Europe.

items: Canada, Ukraine forge 100-year pact built on drones and defence

blocks.text: Two people died when Russian drones hit the Starokozache border crossing between Ukraine and Moldova on Tuesday night, while a "direct threat" to a Polish-Ukrainian crossing point on Wednesday night was only avoided thanks to co-operation between Warsaw and Kyiv, he said.

Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Deutsche Welle, in an interview published Saturday, that he would meet Putin if both leaders were invited to the Group of 20 summit of rich and developing nations in December in Miami.

Putin’s foreign policy adviser, Yuri Ushakov, said Saturday that the possibility of Putin attending the summit had not yet been discussed. The Kremlin in the past has said that Zelenskyy can come to Moscow if he wants a meeting with Putin, a proposal Kyiv has rejected.

articles.title: ‘I love the boldness of modernism’: New York fashion week goes highbrow
articles.summary:
Georgia O’Keeffe inspires the latest Calvin Klein while Michael Kors feels indebted to Alexander Calder

Calvin Klein has taken a highbrow turn in the two years since Veronica Leoni took…

blocks.text: Calvin Klein has taken a highbrow turn in the two years since Veronica Leoni took charge. The Italian designer, a philosophy graduate who was schooled in the chic design studios of Jil Sander and Celine, has shifted away from jeans, boxer shorts and logos, stripping the brand to its minimalist bones: slip dresses and simple coats, slim skirts and crisp T-shirts.

Leoni called this the “discipline of removal”. Her muse this season was Georgia O’Keeffe, an artist who the brand’s namesake founder admired. Klein bought O’Keeffe’s painting Summer Days in 1983 for $1m, subsequently donating it to the Whitney Museum. A checked pattern taken from O’Keeffe’s distinctive capsule wardrobe of utilitarian chic appeared on this catwalk as a wrap coat, hardware-free with a fabric belt and no buttons.

blocks.caption: Veronica Leoni has talked of the ‘discipline of removal’ in new pared back designs for Calvin Klein. Photograph: Calvin Klein

blocks.text: One nod to pop culture was allowed: a model in a crepe-back satin ivory slip dress, her blond hair scraped back by a simple headband, called to mind the late Carolyn Bessette-Kennedy, the iconic Calvin Klein employee who was launched back into the fashion conversation by Ryan Murphy’s Love Story earlier this year.

Over at the Michael Kors show staged in the sunny courtyard of the Museum of Modern Art, the first model was wearing glossy black disc earrings the size of potato crisps suspended from glinting stainless steel hooks. They looked like pieces from Alexander Calder’s huge mobile, Lobster Trap and Fish Tail, which hangs in the stairwell of the museum.

blocks.caption: A model shows off glossy black disc earrings, part of the new Michael Kors collection. Photograph: Michael Kors

blocks.text: No art heist had taken place, but Kors admitted to being indebted to Calder. This summer, the designer travelled with his husband to Paris, where a major Calder retrospective was held. “We were just in love! The magic of it,” Kors enthused at a preview before his show. Modernism became the theme for this latest collection.
after newsletter promotion

As well as the Calder-adjacent earrings, there was an evening dress carved with crescent-shaped edges at the shoulders in homage to Matisse’s cut-outs, and a pencil skirt zigzagged with black and white stripes which winked to Carmen Herrera. A ribbon of banana yellow floating from the hem of a black dress was giving Ellsworth Kelly.

blocks.caption: ‘A ribbon of banana yellow’: some of the clothes on display at the Michael Kors show. Photograph: Julia D’Ambola/BFA.com/Shutterstock

blocks.text: “I love the boldness of modernism and the optimism of it,” Kors said. After the bedazzled glamour of last season’s show, held in the Lincoln Center opera house, this collection leaned into a more artsy sensibility, with traditionally feminine colours swapped out for tobacco, black and moss green.

Held on the 25th anniversary of 9/11, the show was also “a remembrance”, Kors said, and a tribute to the resilience of the city. “We keep going. Everyone said that no one would ever want to live downtown again,” he recalled. “And now look at us.”
Tory Burch has transformed her brand, once synonymous with logoed ballet flats and polished Upper East Side good taste, into one of the most directional names of New York fashion week.

Her show was accompanied by the eerie, unsettling soundtrack from The Shining, because “it’s quite dystopian for all of us right now”, she said backstage. The clothes were a cheerful contrast, opening with a lavender silk dress accessorised with a boa of golden silk feathers.

Jewel-toned pencil skirts, embellished cardigans and ballerina necklines had a midcentury sophistication. “I was thinking about how much people need to feel joy right now. We need to dream and escape, to find bright spots where we can, and that’s where this collection came from.”

articles.title: Christopher Harborne matches £36m Reform donation of Ben Delo
articles.summary:
Party leader, Nigel Farage, says he is humbled by the contributions from cryptocurrency billionaires

The cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne has given £36m to Reform UK, matching…

blocks.text: The cryptocurrency billionaire Christopher Harborne has given £36m to Reform UK, matching a donation from fellow billionaire Ben Delo.
The pledges are jointly the largest donations made to a UK party and are likely to intensify calls for a cap on political donations.
Reform leader, Nigel Farage, said he was “honoured and humbled” by the donations, which come at a time when Reform is facing intense scrutiny regarding its finances.

The Metropolitan police is conducting an inquiry into Reform’s finances, and Farage is facing a parliamentary standards investigation into a £5m gift from Harborne, made before he was first elected an MP in 2024. Reform UK and Farage have denied any wrongdoing.
Farage said: “I am honoured and humbled that Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne have shown such confidence in Reform.

“Both men know that we are the only party that can turn the country around and win the next general election – thanks to their generosity, we are now able to fight that election on a level playing field.”

Harborne said: “There will be a lot of media speculation regarding this donation. So what do I expect in return for my donations? Nothing. No peerage, no policy change, just a party that is ready for government.

“I have already accumulated enough wealth for the rest of my life. I am committed to putting that to work for Britain and humanity as a whole. I want the same as everyone else in Britain: for my children and grandchildren to have the chance to live happy and productive lives here and be rewarded for their hard work.
“At the next general election people will have to vote for the party that they think will best get that done and I’m making a donation very clearly to the party that I believe will do so.”

articles.title: Calls for investigation after video shows ICE officers using batons on protesters
articles.summary:
Residents in Frederick, Maryland, shaken after clashes as activists decry violence from officers as ‘unconscionable’

Political leaders in Maryland are calling for investigations into the…

blocks.text: Political leaders in Maryland are calling for investigations into the conduct of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers as they clashed with protesters during a federal operation in a local community.

Residents of Frederick, a city about 50 miles north-west of Baltimore, are still shaken more than a week after ICE officers arrived in numerous vehicles and could be seen on video footage using batons on members of the public and driving their cars on to the sidewalk towards people.

At one point during the occurrences last Thursday and Friday, approaching the Labor Day weekend, protesters sat down in a line across the road linking arms, and also tried to block the doorway to a residential address as ICE personnel approached. Officers went inside the home but left without appearing to have made any arrests.
Federal officers arrived last Thursday, attracting grassroots activists who watch out in communities and warn people when ICE vehicles or agents are spotted. Protests quickly began and then grew.

Cesar Diaz, the president of Frederick city council, heard news of a confrontation and said he rushed to the scene. He said he had to step out of the way to avoid being hit by an ICE vehicle and saw a colleague, Katie Nash, the vice-president of the council, have to do the same.
“I had to move so I wouldn’t get hit, and the vice-president did too. There was no warning at all. The vehicle was one foot away from her,” Diaz told the Guardian earlier this week.
“We were there to show people that they had our support, and so the officers would see it too,” he said. Diaz estimated around 200 protesters gathered quite quickly, carrying signs and singing.
At that point, four or five ICE vehicles were in the area, he said, a number that grew to eight or nine by last Thursday evening.

Other witnesses reported that some residents were scared to leave their homes and go to work. Some required help to make sure their kids, who were coming off the school bus on Thursday afternoon, would be safe walking home.
Protesters can be heard on video footage of the demonstration chanting “Go home”, “Leave Frederick” and “Leave Maryland” at the gathered federal personnel.

blocks.caption: Protesters sit on road to block ICE in Frederick, MD

blocks.text: ICE said in a statement to local media that they were in the area in “an effort to arrest a man” during a vehicle stop last Thursday morning but the man fled the scene, the Frederick News-Post reported. After that more ICE officers arrived and tensions escalated.

In the evening, ICE officers confronted protesters by driving their vehicles towards them, as seen in bystander footage, and videos shared by the Hagerstown Rapid Response activist group also showed officers approaching a home. It was then that some protestors tried to stop them from reaching the building by creating a human chain, and violence erupted.
Officers in tactical vests can be seen raising batons and hitting at least one protester about their body, while others are dragged and shoved.

“The level of violence went beyond what the situation called for. It was too much. It exceeded what is permitted,” Diaz said, saying that at least two people had to go to the hospital due to injuries. “There are many other options when dealing with unarmed people.”
He called for an investigation, as did Congresswoman April McClain Delaney, whose district includes the city, calling the incidents deeply concerning.

In a statement, Delaney said: “No family should be afraid to leave their home or feel unsafe in their own neighborhood … I am especially disturbed by reports that ICE agents used force against Frederick residents. These allegations demand immediate answers and a full, transparent investigation.”
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), the parent agency of ICE, did not respond to a request for comment from the Guardian.
In an earlier statement to local network WBAL-TV, the agency declined to comment “for operation security” and “the safety” of their personnel.
DHS told the outlet that “criminal illegal aliens are not welcome in the US”.
Frederick authorities said they were not aware of any ICE or local arrests. Frederick police said personnel were dispatched to try to de-escalate the situation.
Police chief Kevin Meyer said his officers asked ICE whether they had an arrest warrant but that federal officers refused to discuss it.

Soolah Kemp, a member of Hagerstown Rapid Response, said she was recording video when an ICE car drove in her direction. “I heard the siren, I turned, and he was coming at me. He sped up, so I jumped out of the way. He had enough room on the street to not have an issue. He didn’t have to do what he did,” she said.

blocks.caption: ICE vehicle driven on pavement toward protesters

blocks.text: She has filed a report of the incident with the state attorney general’s office, she said.

US senator Chris Van Hollen has demanded an immediate investigation into events and said “[Donald] Trump’s ICE operations are not about making our country safer, they are about creating chaos and instilling fear in our communities”.
Tatiana Santos, of the activist network Indivisible Frederick Forward, said that the ICE conduct she witnessed was “unconscionable”.
“These people were so peaceful in the defense of their immigrant neighbors. They were simply standing and chanting things like: ‘We shall not be moved,’” she said.
She has asked Maryland governor Wes Moore to speak out and called for him to conduct an investigation.
Moore’s office said in a statement the governor was working with local leaders to “address what happened and make sure that there is real accountability”.
Lex McMenamin contributed reporting

articles.title: Trump visits Ireland, says unification would be 'fantastic'
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump's trip to Ireland to watch a golf tournament has also included meetings with leaders there.

image.caption: Trump (in blue suit) received a military welcome upon arrivalImage: Kylie Cooper/REUTERS

blocks.text: US President Donald Trump has said he would "love" to see the Republic of Ireland, an EU member, unite with British-run ⁠Northern Ireland as he faced reporters' questions on a range of issues on Saturday.

Trump is taking the weekend trip largely to watch the Irish Open golf tournament held on a course he owns on the country’s Atlantic coast, but he met as well with the Irish president and prime minister, or taoiseach.
The US leader also spoke optimistically about his country's war with Iran and its trade conflict with Canada, among several other topics.
What did Trump say about Ireland?

After a meeting with Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin in the capital, Dublin, Trump said he very much supported what he said would be the eventual unification of the two parts of the island of Ireland.
"Well, I don't want to ​cause any problems, ​but ‌I will tell you, I'd love to see ‌it unified," Trump told ‌reporters.
"The way I look at it, it's ⁠going ​to happen ​eventually ... I think it would ​be a ‌fantastic thing," he added.
"Now the UK will have ​something ⁠to say about it ... but ⁠I think ​it would be a great thing."

The British government responded swiftly to the remarks, with Prime Minister Andy Burham's office saying that in his view, there was no majority public support for a referendum on the issue and that there would not be another one until that changed.

Previous US presidents have avoided touching on the subject in view of the delicate nature of the issue, with Northern Ireland seeing decades of of deadly sectarian violence in the 20th century over the question of whom it should belong to.

blocks.caption: Micheal Martin (L) has led Ireland twice since 2020Image: Brendan Smialowski/AFP

blocks.text: What did Trump say about the Iran war?
Trump also said that the US war with Iran, which began on February 28, would "end very soon" — a view he has frequently expressed in the past without it becoming reality.
He also said that the end of the conflict would mean that the price of oil, which has soared as a result of the war, would "come tumbling down."
However, he vehemently defended his decision to mount the military operation against Iran.
He said that the US attacked because "Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon", adding: "They were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon."

"If they had it, they would have blown up Israel, they would have blown up the Middle East, and they would have hit some [...] in my opinion, [of] Europe's cities and beyond cities, and they would probably hit us soon before we put out the fire. But they cannot have a nuclear weapon."
The war with Iran is not supported by a majority of the US population, particularly in view of promises made by Trump on the campaign trail to keep his country out of foreign "forever" conflicts.

blocks.caption: Trump and Martin held talks in Farmleigh House in Phoenix Park in DublinImage: Brendan Smialowski/AFP

blocks.text: What did Trump say about Canada?
The president sounded a similarly optimistic note regarding the US trade war with Canada.
He said Canada was keen to make a deal and that one could be struck "fairly soon," while reiterating his claims that Canada had treated US farmers unfairly with its tariffs.
"Canada ‌wants to make a ‌deal ​very badly," he said.
"Canada has ​to treat our farmers better. ​They can't ‌charge our farmers tariffs," he said, ​adding: "You'll ⁠probably see a deal with Canada ⁠fairly ​soon."

articles.title: Uganda lays 'boy king' Oyo to rest amid succession row
articles.summary: A funeral is underway for King Oyo Nyimba, who was crowned in the Tooro Kingdom in 1995 aged just 3. His death at 34 has triggered a dispute over a successor, as rumors abound of possible heirs born…

image.caption: The funeral has been taking place of King Oyo Nyimba, seen here aged 18 in 2010Image: Marc Hofer/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Uganda has concluded a nine-day period of mourning for King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, with a funeral for the Tooro Kingdom's late monarch due to take place in the western city of Fort Portal on Saturday.

Oyo, who once held the unofficial title of the world's youngest king, ascended the throne as a young child in 1995 and died last month of cancer aged just 34, with his death prompting a bitter succession dispute.

blocks.caption: Oyo's coffin lay in state at the Karuziika Royal PalaceImage: Michael Muhati/REUTERS

blocks.text: How is Oyo to be laid to rest?

The casket carrying the king's body, which was draped in the blue-and-yellow Tooro flag, was carried by hearse from the royal palace in Fort Portal in a procession accompanied by royal guards dressed in orange tunics and beating wooden sticks.
The ceremony in St. John's Cathedral was to be attended by hundreds of mourners, including senior Ugandan government officials.
After the service in the cathedral, Oyo was to be buried at the site of the royal tombs.
At the burial ceremony, tradition dictates that the successor should throw nine coffee berries into the grave.

blocks.caption: Oyo's death has caused widespread griefImage: Abubaker Lubowa/REUTERS

blocks.text: Dispute over Oyo's successor
However, the question of that successor has aroused considerable controversy, and it was in doubt until late on Friday who would carry out that rite.
On Wednesday, a committee made up of members of the royal clan announced it had chosen Oyo's cousin, Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma, as the new king.
Kijanangoma, 54, is a news anchor and editor at state broadcaster UBC.
But the immediate family of the late king said that the latter's will had called for a son who was born out of wedlock and has yet to be identified to succeed him.
Additionally, there have been claims on social media that there are at least two possible heirs alleged to be Oyo's children.
Those supporting Kijanangoma say Oyo's family has so far failed to come up with concrete information on the alleged son, while traditionalists also favor the choice of an adult as new monarch.
A source with knowledge ⁠of ​crisis talks on the matter said authorities had managed to get Kijanangoma officially accepted as successor on Friday.

blocks.caption: Mourners queued before the royal palace to view the king's bodyImage: Abubaker Lubowa/REUTERS

blocks.text: Beloved traditional monarchs
Queen Mother Best Kemigisa said in a statement that the succession battle undermined the family's ability to mourn the king's death.
"I also appeal to those fighting over the throne: Please, there will be time for all of that," she said. "Let us grieve and bury my son King Oyo."

Although Uganda is led by an elected head of state, it still possesses several kingdoms that were restored in 1993 after being banned for some three decades following the country's independence from British colonial rule.
The monarchs of such kingdoms are often beloved but hold no formal power. Instead they are seen as guardians of traditional identity and heritage.

articles.title: Russian GRU spies behind failed Leipzig attack: reports
articles.summary: A German newspaper has cited reports tying a failed attack at Leipzig Airport to Moscow's GRU military intelligence agency. One suspect's ties to GRU were known when he entered the country, yet he…

image.caption: Bomb experts were able to disarm an explosives-laden drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport in a failed attack now definitively attributed to Russia's GRU military intelligence agencyImage: Axel Schmidt/REUTERS

blocks.text: Germany's Welt am Sonntag (WaS) newspaper has cited intelligence reports tying the recent failed drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport directly to Moscow's GRU military intelligence agency.
In an article published on Saturday, Welt am Sonntag said that a man with known ties to the GRU was responsible for operational logistics in the attempted attack.
Further, it said those ties were known to German authorities when the man entered the country from Turkey, nevertheless, he was not surveilled after arrival.
Classified security assessments cited by the paper say the Russian national is now in his home country after departing to Serbia on a flight from Berlin-Brandenburg Airport.
A second man, a Belarus citizen, was also cited as an accomplice in the report.
Germany blames Russia for attempted terror attack in Leipzig
Explosives thought to have entered Germany from Bulgaria and Serbia

German intelligence sources said that the explosives used in the incident were likely smuggled into Germany via truck from Bulgaria and Serbia and then stored in underground depots once they arrived in Leipzig.

Berlin quickly made clear that forensic evidence found at Leipzig/Halle Airport — including drone configuration, explosives and trigger mechanisms used in other Russian hybrid attacks — pointed to a Russian plot.

In early August, German tabloid BILD reported that authorities had found DNA traces on the drone's remote control antenna. Those samples were said to have matched DNA found at the scene of a July 20, 2024, arson attack at a Leipzig logistics facility operated by German courier company DHL.
Leipzig attack averted but Russian escalation will continue

The incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport — a hub for military aid destined for Ukraine — occurred on the evening of August 4 and involved an explosives-laden drone that was found near a Ukrainian transport jet.
Authorities were able to disarm the drone and after public speculation that Moscow was behind the incident the German government officially blamed Russia in early September.
Saturday's article said Berlin made the attribution on the basis of the intelligence reports cited.
In response to its conclusion, Germany announced the closure of the Russian Consulate General in Bonn.
The Kremlin in turn reacted by closing Goethe Institutes — a German cultural exchange outfit — across Russia.
As in numerous similar hybrid attacks prior, Russia has denied any involvement in the incident.
Putin denies Russian involvement in Leipzig drone attack

articles.title: NBI uncovers POC reimbursement, delayed payment for 2019 SEA Games cauldron
articles.summary: The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has uncovered additional details in its investigation into the controversial 2019 Southeast Asian Games (SEA Games) cauldron, including what it described as…

blocks.text: Published September 12, 2026 7:25pm

The National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) has uncovered additional details in its investigation into the controversial 2019 Southeast Asian Games (SEA Games) cauldron, including what it described as a questionable reimbursement involving the Philippine Olympic Committee (POC) and the Philippine Southeast Asian Games Organizing Committee (PHISGOC).

In an exclusive interview in Pasay City, NBI Director Melvin Matibag said investigators found that, aside from the alleged double payment, PHISGOC also received reimbursement from the POC. Matibag said the transaction is now being questioned because the money paid by the POC came from public funds, while PHISGOC is a non-government organization (NGO).
Matibag also said the payment for the cauldron appeared to have been made only as an “afterthought,” noting that it was reportedly settled years after the Philippines hosted the 2019 SEA Games.
The NBI further discovered that the component of the cauldron responsible for producing the flame was rented rather than purchased.
While the cauldron has long been reported to have cost P55 million, Matibag said documents obtained by the NBI show that less than P50 million was actually paid for it.

Following the testimony of a witness who surfaced on Monday, the NBI said it will issue subpoenas to additional personalities as investigators continue to look into the newly disclosed details surrounding the cauldron’s procurement and payment.
The NBI is investigating the alleged anomalous procurement of projects related to the 2019 SEA Games after receiving new information and documents involving PHISGOC. — VBL, GMA News
