articles.title: Jamaican delegation defends legal route of petition to King Charles for slavery reparations
articles.summary:
Petition to king, who remains Jamaica’s head of state, is formally lodged in landmark visit to UK by officials

A palpable surge of emotion swept through Brixton’s New Park Road Baptist…

blocks.text: A palpable surge of emotion swept through Brixton’s New Park Road Baptist church as the packed congregation rose to sing Bob Marley’s Redemption Song.
The service on Sunday marked the anniversary of the 1781 Zong massacre, when more than 100 enslaved Africans were thrown overboard so the ship’s owners could claim insurance for “lost cargo”.

And the song – a lament for the horrors of transatlantic slavery and a tribute to the resilience of those who fought for freedom – set the tone for a landmark visit to the UK by Jamaican officials to petition King Charles over reparations for slavery.

The petition, backed by leaders of other Caribbean nations, asks the monarch to request legal advice from the privy council, the final court of appeal for UK overseas territories and some Commonwealth countries.

It asks Charles, who is still Jamaica’s head of state, to seek guidance on three questions: whether the forced transport of Africans to Jamaica was lawful; whether it constituted a crime against humanity; and whether Britain is under an obligation to provide restitution for slavery and its enduring consequences.
Led by the culture minister, Olivia Grange, the Jamaican delegation included lawyers and members of the country’s national council on reparations.
The delegation met diaspora communities, UK politicians, church leaders and institutions – including the British Museum, from which Jamaica is seeking the return of artefacts.
Grange also held talks with the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, though sources say these were not focused on reparations.

blocks.caption: Olivia Grange, Jamaica’s culture minister, took part in a service at a Brixton church during her delegation’s visit to London.  Photograph: Alberto Pezzali/AP

blocks.text: Jamaica’s petition has ignited a fierce debate about the legality of transatlantic slavery and political implications. The former privy council member Lord Sumption dismissed the legal strategy as “nonsense” and argued that the issue was “not a question of law at all” but one of morals and politics. Jamaican experts have defended the legality of the petition.

Speaking at a briefing for UK parliamentarians, Edward Fitzgerald KC insisted Jamaica was acting in accordance with a little‑used mechanism in the Judicial Committee Act 1833 which allows the king to refer questions of “legal or constitutional nature” to the privy council when they cannot be resolved through ordinary courts.
Harj Narulla, a member of the UK team of counsels, told the Guardian it was an “obvious jurisdictional route”.

“It was quite clear you can’t do a judicial review, for example, of some government decision … The issue is with the state itself, with the United Kingdom, which is the state responsible for slavery in Jamaica,” he said.

Ulele Burnham, another member of the UK legal team, added: “The petition argues that the atrocities, the forced uprooting, the violent subjugation for profit was of course immoral, everyone knows that. But the petition’s very focus is to show that it was also clearly inconsistent with the law of the time. Non-Europeans did not suddenly become human when slavery ended. They always were. And even in those days, humans had some rights in English and international law.”

In Jamaica, though the pursuit of reparations is supported by the two main parties, members of the opposition People’s National party raised concerns that the delegation had not managed to secure a meeting with the king. Grange said a meeting with Charles “was not part of the plan”.

“Before we came to London, we had consulted with both the Palace and the privy council to confirm the correct legal process for filing the petition. Both confirmed the correct process was to file it by post and email, which is what we did,” she said.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: Bell Ribeiro-Addy, the MP for Clapham and Brixton Hill in London, said the Jamaicans were ‘enacting their rights under English law’.  Photograph: Bell Ribeiro-Addy

blocks.text: The Labour MP Bell Ribeiro‑Addy, the chair of the all‑party parliamentary group for Afrikan Reparations, said Jamaica was well within its rights to petition the monarch. “Due to colonialism, which obviously initially had its root in enslavement, there are certain responsibilities that [the UK] has. We don’t get the privilege of still having Jamaica as part of the realm … without them also in turn having the right to petition King Charles. They are enacting their rights under English law and they have the right to ask those questions,” she said.
In December 2024, Jamaica’s government tabled a bill in parliament to remove the king as the country’s head of state. The bill has not progressed to becoming a law.

Pointing to recent global momentum – including 123 nations voting for a UN resolution describing chattel slavery as the gravest crime against humanity – Ribeiro‑Addy said it was time for Britain to confront its past and the decisions that continue to shape the present.

She described headlines quoting huge reparation figures (which were not mentioned in the Jamaican petition) as a distraction. “What seems to happen a lot when we talk about reparations is people want to distract people with figures,” she said. “They divorce themselves from the reality of what we are talking about. No one is saying that reparative justice will never include any sort of payment. But that is never the starting point. And we have to remember that this country refuses to even apologise. This country refuses to do the things that it can do, which don’t cost any money at all.

“The enslavement of peoples of African descent … meant that anybody who was not white was considered less than … almost being classified as not quite human. And that is a serious issue. If we are ever going to challenge racism properly, we have to get down to its very root.”

As the delegation lodged the petition on Monday, a spokesperson for the prime minister, Andy Burnham, reiterated the British government’s long‑held position that “the UK does not and will not pay reparations”.

Ribeiro‑Addy said it would be an insult to African and Caribbean countries if Britain refuses to discuss reparations at the upcoming Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Antigua, which the king is scheduled to attend.

“We’re meant to no longer be a group of countries under an empire. We were meant to be a group of countries with a shared history and who are treated as equals,” she said. “The idea that all of the countries bar one want to have a discussion and so the discussion is stopped has to be wrong … if we do things like that, I think we will soon see the crumbling of the Commonwealth. And that would be a huge shame.”

articles.title: Registered sex offender was allowed to participate at South Carolina church for decades
articles.summary:
The Brookwood Church in Simpsonville only just disqualified Jerry Sidell from serving there in any capacity

A registered sex offender who was sentenced to prison in the 1980s after he told…

blocks.text: A registered sex offender who was sentenced to prison in the 1980s after he told authorities that he had molested several boys whom he met through his religious work with Christian youth in Georgia was later allowed to participate for decades in ministry at a South Carolina church.

The Brookwood church, a southern Baptist institution in the South Carolina city of Simpsonville, only just disqualified Jerry Sidell from serving there in any capacity, after he joined it in 1999 and fulfilled various ministerial roles.

The church’s senior pastor, Bryan Jones, told congregants at a Thursday night meeting that Sidell had been “forthright” with Brookwood leaders back then about his previously pleading guilty in Georgia to the crimes of enticing a minor for indecent purposes and child molestation.

Without mentioning Sidell’s name, Jones said that church leaders implemented boundaries addressing his participation at Brookwood, which operates a preschool. Jones said those rules included a prohibition from working in or being around children or student ministries.

Sidell, 69, also could not set foot in the school or those particular ministries’ spaces, Jones said. And Sidell had to disclose his past to those in charge of any non-children or non-student ministries in which he wanted to take part, Jones told congregants, according to an audio recording of the meeting provided to the Guardian.
Yet Jones – who was named Brookwood’s senior pastor in late 2022 – also suggested that he personally had only recently learned of Sidell’s status as a registered sex offender.

Jones didn’t elaborate. But he said he reacted to that discovery by meeting Sidell and informing him that he could no longer perform with the church’s adult musical band or be a member of the small prayer group – also made up of adults – to which he belonged.

Jones also said Brookwood had enacted a new policy requiring “any” registered sex offender attending church services to enter through a specific door, check in with the institution’s security team and then sit with a designated guard. That designated guard would then escort the registered sex offender out of Brookwood after the completion of services, Jones said.
As Jones put it, he and his fellow Brookwood leaders believe in “grace and forgiveness” – but, he added, “we felt … there are consequences for actions”.

An email to the Guardian from an individual familiar with Brookwood and Sidell contended that the church specifically put those heightened rules in place in either July or August. That was after authorities in Pawleys Island, South Carolina, reported arresting a registered sex offender named Warren Spence Perry for allegedly violating his probation by working at a school and children’s daycare run by a local southern Baptist church.

Five other people connected to the Pawleys Island community church and its school, about four hours away from Simpsonville by car, were later also arrested on suspicion of illegally concealing Perry’s involvement with children there.

Perry, 70, pleaded guilty in 2023 to sexually exploiting a minor three years earlier, and a proposed federal class-action lawsuit has been filed at the church and school where he had been working, as WCIV and other South Carolina news outlets have reported.

Furthermore, the individual who emailed the Guardian about Sidell accurately noted his having founded Rusty Bucket Music, a venue which – according to social media video and images – has hosted youth performers and patrons since its opening in 2019.

Videos available online suggest Brookwood leaders have had a presence at Rusty Bucket Music in the South Carolina town of Gray Court, which is adjacent to Simpsonville. Two videos show Jones and his fellow Brookwood pastor JC Thompson delivering prepared, recorded discussions of biblical scripture there.
Rusty Bucket Music’s website and its Facebook page had been taken down as of Friday.

A professional networking page under Sidell’s name described him as a Brookwood church musician since at least 2013. He reportedly partook in worship ministry, played the keyboard and participated in small men’s groups at Brookwood, according to the Christian church watchdog website MinistryWatch, which first reported on Sidell in late August.

The individual who corresponded with the Guardian about Sidell said the Brookwood church has about 5,000 congregants. According to the individual, “Sidell’s sex offender status was not disclosed to many of the people” who served alongside him or encountered him at the ministries in which he was involved.
As the individual put it: “Sidell kept this information extremely private.”
Sidell did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Neither did Brookwood.
after newsletter promotion
At Thursday’s meeting with congregants, Thompson and Jones made it a point to say that their own children were Brookwood congregants, too.
“We care about protecting our people,” said Thompson, who also said that Brookwood had security cameras throughout the entirety of its campus, among other safety measures.
Another pastor, Matt Plunkett, said all church volunteers must also take an abuse-prevention class.

Jones at one point asked the congregation to pray for victims. But at another juncture, in a clear allusion to Sidell and the media’s interest in him, he asserted: “Satan would love to disrupt what’s happening in this church. He would love to disrupt what God is doing in this church.”

The cases centering on Sidell and Perry came amid a broader, years-long scandal involving the handling of matters related to sexual abuse by the Southern Baptist Convention (SBC), the US’s largest Protestant denomination. It is also the second-largest Christian denomination in the US behind the Roman Catholic church.

The SBC, a politically influential group of loosely affiliated churches with about 12 million congregants, in June 2022 issued a 205-page document listing hundreds of Baptist leaders and congregants accused or found guilty of sexually abusing children.
Neither Sidell nor Perry were named in that specific document.

Other religious denominations in the US and across the world besides the SBC and the Roman Catholic church – Christian or otherwise – have also spent years grappling with sexual abuse within their ranks.
With respect to his case, Sidell pleaded guilty in 1983 to five charges of child molestation and one of enticing a minor to commit indecent acts, a 1986 Atlanta Journal-Constitution article reported.

The newspaper reported that Sidell at one point told detectives that he had molested nine boys whom he knew from serving at the nondenominational First Christian church of Jonesboro, Georgia, as a youth minister. He received six concurrent 10-year prison sentences, the Journal-Constitution reported.

The parents of two of Sidell’s victims – a pair of brothers – sued Sidell for $2m. The Journal-Constitution reported that the younger son secured a $500,000 jury verdict, but the award was eliminated entirely after Sidell was granted a new trial on what the outlet termed a legal technicality. The plaintiffs then dropped the litigation, and told the Journal-Constitution that members of their church ostracized them for going public against Sidell.

In addition to South Carolina, Sidell is registered as a sex offender in Florida, a US justice department tool shows. Both registrations list a home address in Simpsonville about a mile and a half away from the Brookwood church.

articles.title: Beyond the heatwave: what it really takes for climate warnings to cut through in the UK
articles.summary:
As trust in institutions wavers, experts say local, collective action is more effective in driving change

Wildfires, excess deaths, hosepipe bans, school closures: this summer many British…

blocks.text: Wildfires, excess deaths, hosepipe bans, school closures: this summer many British people have experienced the often devastating effects of the climate crisis in ways they had not before. In that sense, policymakers and climate experts have a unique opportunity to engage with the public about what needs to happen to better prepare the country for the years ahead. But as trust in institutions wavers – and yellowed, drought-stricken grass begins to recover – can the messaging cut through?

This week, reflecting on a summer as “hot as hell”, the UN’s head of climate, Simon Stiell, said: “Climate is sometimes seen as a partisan issue, as territory in the culture wars. That is palpably false.”

He said: “Climate cuts across the core concerns of voters, whatever their politics: [affecting] family health, community safety and economic stability; affordable food and available water; jobs, business costs and household bills.”

In policy terms, there are two ways to lessen the impact: climate mitigation and climate adaptation. Mitigation involves reducing the emissions causing global heating, while adaptation is about responding to its impacts. For climate experts and policymakers, the distinction is important.

But recent research conducted by Climate Outreach, a charity specialising in climate communication research, found that people in the UK do not generally divide climate action into these two categories. “People talk about them interchangeably,” said Chris Pollard, a senior researcher at Climate Outreach. Only about half of those in the study understood the term “climate adaptation”.

However, the mixed response to the government-issued “severe alert” to wildfire risk in mid-August highlighted the need for clearer communication on both. While some recipients of the notification decried the top-down “overreach”, others complained the government should instead be focusing on decarbonising the energy grid.

As the impacts of the climate crisis become more immediate, the question is not only whether people understand the difference, but whether their understanding leads to action and support for policies that tackle both.

blocks.caption: Smoke rises from wildfires near Dunwich Heath in Suffolk. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA

blocks.text: “What people are wanting is: what works, and how they do it,” said Rowena Hill, a professor of resilience, emergencies and disaster science at Nottingham Trent University.

But there is a fine line to tread when it comes to responsibility. The recent £75m Let’s Save Water campaign, which advised people to treat water as a precious resource and cut their daily use by 28 litres, prompted questions about whether this put too much responsibility on consumers, given that a huge contributor to water loss is ageing infrastructure and a lack of investment in the water system.
“Empowerment is really hindered because of that lack of clear accountability,” Hill said. The “you are responsible” needed to become “we are responsible”, she added.

And how do you make sure that people trust the message? Accountability matters, but confidence in political institutions is low, with research suggesting that elected representatives misperceive public support for climate policies. More than a third of Britons surveyed by Ipsos this summer said the Labour government had done a “bad job” dealing with the climate crisis since coming into power in July 2024.

Trust also comes from making climate risks relevant to people’s lives. “It is about the community understanding the community’s risks, rather than the community understanding how they might fit into this really big geography of a risk analysis,” Hill said. “The value of our environmental surroundings, how people use that and what that means to the local community is really important.”
The response to the felling of the Sycamore Gap tree offers one example: the grief and anger that followed demonstrated people’s strong connection to their immediate environment.
after newsletter promotion

blocks.caption: The Sycamore Gap tree in 2008. Photograph: Murdo Macleod/The Guardian

blocks.text: Climate Outreach uses the seven British segments produced by More in Common to understand how people’s values differ, and where messages can resonate across groups. As Pollock puts it, messaging should focus on “things that cut across values” using framings that “appeal to as many people as possible and do not alienate”.

In a time of culture wars, this advice is not just theoretical. Greener Henley, a climate and nature-based action charity, is using it. “We’re appealing to people across the political spectrum,” said Kate Oldridge, the charity’s executive director. The charity used research on the segmentation of the local community to tailor its pledges, inviting people to commit to simple, practical actions that are “very relevant to people’s lives”.

Oldbridge said this approach could drive tangible change beyond the community. “It also serves to inspire by demonstrating to policymakers that here’s a community that can do something really amazing,” she said. For example, the charity is working with schools to implement climate action plans recommended by the government, including offering practical help to keep classrooms cool in summer and better defend playgrounds against flooding.

For the volunteers, taking part provides a sense of hope and collective purpose. Oldbridge said: “They see that there’s a problem. They want to do something, but it also brings them joy to get out there and do something. It makes them feel more hopeful, more inspired.
“We feel massively supported and our anxiety alleviated by the fact that we’re actually doing this work and doing it with each other.”

articles.title: Heatwaves hit the Sunday roast: why the RHS says cauliflower is off the menu
articles.summary:
Charity urges gardeners in England to swap thirsty brassicas for drought-tolerant crops

They are an integral part of the British Sunday roast – but cauliflowers are now going to be off the…

blocks.text: They are an integral part of the British Sunday roast – but cauliflowers are now going to be off the menu, according to the Royal Horticultural Society.
England’s climate has changed so much that the RHS is now recommending that gardeners exclude the brassicas from their vegetable patches.
The UK is expecting a poor harvest of most brassicas, such as broccoli, cauliflower and cabbages, owing to the drought, with farmers saying this year could be one of the worst on record.

This summer was the UK’s hottest on record, according to provisional Met Office data. In England, temperatures peaked at 38.1C (100.1F) at Kew Gardens in London on 13 August, and June had already been confirmed as the country’s hottest since records began in 1884.
Scientists have said these heatwaves are only possible because of the climate crisis, predominantly caused by burning of fossil fuels.

The RHS says home gardeners should stop growing cauliflower because of the change to the climate, adding many of its horticulturalists had stopped a long time before as planting cauliflowers had been so unsuccessful.

The charity said cauliflowers and their close relative capabrese were thirsty and easily stressed in high temperatures, in which they fail to form a decent head. It recommends gardeners also reconsider planting other vegetables in the brassica family such as cabbages and brussels sprouts.

blocks.caption: Cauliflower cheese may soon no longer feature in the British roast dinner. Photograph: Felicity Cloake/The Guardian

blocks.text: Guy Barter, the RHS’s chief horticulturist, said: “Cauliflowers and their brassica cousins have been the hardest hit of those commonly found in domestic veg patches, and with summers likely to follow recent patterns, swapping them out for an equally as flavourful and nutritious alternative will save on all-important watering and provide a better guarantee of a good harvest.

“There’s no doubt that we’re set to see tomatoes continue as the most popular summer vegetable, but with the likes of Asian loofah and okra cropping up more at mealtimes. Hopefully with recent rains we will see winter crops, carrots, leeks and brussels sprouts, make a recovery this year.”
Horticulturalists in the charity’s gardens said they had been experimenting with alternatives to cauliflower.

Simone Bratt, who tends the kitchen gardens at RHS Bridgewater, said she had not grown cauliflower for “a few years”. Growth had been “very hit and miss with the extremes of weather and we would only grow them as a late crop”, she said.

“We tried a spring sowing again this year, but the heat really won. They bolted before we even got them in the ground. They simply haven’t been able to cope with the severity of the conditions, and need a lot of water and cool conditions.”

Bratt added that purple sprouting broccoli was a good swap for cauliflower. “They also should cope much better as a ‘cut and come’ crop, rather than waiting for a single full head of calabrese or cauliflower.”

blocks.caption: Gardeners will have to start rethinking what to plant. Photograph: Karen Robinson/The Observer

blocks.text: The gardening charity said its members said the heat this year had allowed tomatoes and peppers to thrive outdoors, and that melon and watermelon could now be grown outside in some parts of the country, and where their watering needs could be met.
Some gardeners have swapped from cauliflower to kale, as some kale is perennial, with deeper roots, so can better survive droughts.

Gardeners have been able to grow cucumbers and sweet potatoes outside successfully, said Liz Mooney, a horticulturist on the edibles team at RHS Garden Wisley, in Surrey. She added she had not grown cauliflower this year, focusing instead on “warmth-loving crops”.
Cat Hood, a horticulturist at RHS Hyde Hall in Chelmsford, Essex, said she had been experimenting with a range of warmer-climate vegetables, including chillies and okra.

“We’ve had some really strong results from a number of crops this year,” she said. “Chillies, peppers and aubergines have all performed well in the outdoor beds, and we’ve had an amazing crop of loofah in the glasshouse. The okra have also done well, as have tortarello and carosello, the Italian heirloom cucumber-melons. A real surprise has been the yard-long beans, which have given us the best crop I’ve seen since I’ve been here, which I assume is because of the heat.”

articles.summary: A morning fire left 42 families homeless after it swept through Sitio Verde, Barangay San Isidro, Talisay City, on Saturday, September 12.... Keep on reading: Talisay fire leaves 42 families…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines —A morning fire left 42 families homeless after it swept through Sitio Verde, Barangay San Isidro, Talisay City, on Saturday, September 12.
According to the Talisay City Fire Station, the blaze started around 8 a.m. at the residence of a certain Antonio Saberon.
The fire quickly escalated, reaching a 3rd alarm before firefighters managed to bring it under control around 9:02 a.m.
Man sustains burns
Authorities reported that 37 houses were razed while five others sustained partial damage.
The incident left an estimated ₱1.3 million in property damage.
Meanwhile, a 41-year-old man sustained minor burns and was immediately given first aid and medical attention.
Investigators from the Bureau of Fire Protection are still conducting a probe to determine the exact cause of the fire.

articles.title: Xi Jinping gets red carpet at Brics summit amid thaw in India-China relations
articles.summary:
Chinese president’s arrival in Delhi seen as step towards reconciliation after deadly 2020 military clash

The Chinese president, Xi Jinping, has received a red-carpet welcome in India for a…

blocks.text: The Chinese president, Xi Jinping, has received a red-carpet welcome in India for a summit of Brics developing nations, as regional rivals Beijing and Delhi make a public display of thawing relations while quietly competing to lead at a time of shaky US global dominance.
As Xi stepped off the plane, he was walked past an honour guard of Indian soldiers and traditional dancers in colourful dresses.

The Russian president, Vladimir Putin, and Iranian president, Masoud Pezeshkian, had already been welcomed by the Indian prime minister, Narendra Modi, who is hosting one of the group’s most closely watched gatherings since its inception.

The summit marks Xi’s first visit to India in seven years and is seen as the biggest step towards reconciliation after a deadly 2020 military clash along the disputed Himalayan border, in which ‌20 Indian and four Chinese soldiers were killed.

Ties between the nuclear-armed Asian giants have been warming recently, with flights and high-level contacts gradually being restored. China was “willing” to work with India to properly manage differences and be “good neighbours and friends”, China’s foreign ministry said on Friday.

Leaders and diplomats have been convening in India for the annual gathering of the Brics grouping, named after five of its earliest members – Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa – that was conceived as a counterweight to western dominance.
This summit comes as wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, along with rising US-China tensions, test the bloc’s ability to find common ground.

Since its inception in 2009, Brics has expanded as a forum for major emerging economies to include Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The group now rivals the US-dominated G7 forum of advanced economies, accounting for half of the global population.

But its growth has also created new fractures and disunity – Iran was bombing Saudi Arabia and the UAE earlier this year, and Brics foreign ministers failed to agree on a joint statement when they met in Delhi in May.
Reuters reported on Saturday that India’s summit would result in a generic joint declaration that would show unity by condemning unilateral war, but ⁠was unlikely to ​name any single country.
Jiang Shixue, vice-president of the expert committee of the China thinktank Council for BRICs cooperation (China), said the 11 members “cannot speak with one voice on many issues”.
“The only solution is to continuously strengthen political consensus,” he told the South China Morning Post.
Beijing and Delhi have differing views on the role of the group.

China has sought to expand Brics power as a counterweight to the US under Donald Trump’s leadership, which has launched global tariff and trade wars and retreated from multilateral institutions such as the UN, which afforded it international credibility.
India has taken a more cautious approach, seeing Brics as a bridge between the west and the developing world.

Chietigj Bajpaee, a senior research fellow for South Asia in the Asia-Pacific programme at Chatham House, said this week that Delhi had found it hard to maintain its policy of “strategic hedging” during such a disruptive US presidency.

“India’s position can appear out of sync in a forum whose membership includes countries with more overtly anti-western agendas, including China, Russia and Iran. And two other Brics countries, South Africa and Brazil, have suffered high-profile diplomatic disputes with the US,” he wrote.
“The challenge for Delhi is that it wishes to promote this worldview in a way that is non-western but not explicitly anti-western.”
Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

articles.title: Rapper Lil Durk acquitted of murder-for-hire at Los Angeles trial
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES — A federal jury on Friday, Sept. 11, found rapper Lil Durk not guilty of the attempted killing for hire of rival rapper Quando Rondo at a Los Angeles gas station, a shooting that…

blocks.text: LOS ANGELES — A federal jury on Friday, Sept. 11, found rapper Lil Durk not guilty of the attempted killing for hire of rival rapper Quando Rondo at a Los Angeles gas station, a shooting that resulted in the death of Rondo’s cousin.

The jury deliberated for three days before acquitting Lil Durk, the 33-year-old Grammy-winning Chicago hip-hop artist best known for the 2023 hit “All My Life,” of conspiracy, stalking resulting in death and murder for hire.

Durk supporters including music stars Machine Gun Kelly and Ye — the artist formerly known as Kanye West — appeared in the audience during the two-week trial in downtown Los Angeles. Big groups of fans, livestreamers and other content creators gathered outside the courthouse.

Durk’s co-defendants Deandre Wilson and David Lindsey were convicted of conspiracy to commit stalking, stalking using a dangerous weapon and stalking resulting in death. But both were also acquitted of murder for hire.

“We thank the jury for seeing there was no murder for hire,” Wilson’s attorney Craig Harbaugh said in an email. “We are confident the remaining counts will not survive our pending motion for acquittal.”
Attorneys for Durk and Lindsey did not immediately respond to emails seeking comment.
Durk, whose legal name is Durk Banks, remained in custody, pending a forthcoming trial on a racketeering count that was severed from this trial. He has been jailed since his 2024 arrest.

Prosecutors had alleged that Durk paid to have Rondo killed after someone from Rondo’s entourage fatally shot rapper King Von, a close friend of Durk’s and a member of his Only The Family hip-hop collective, at an Atlanta nightclub in 2020.

The prosecution alleged that in August 2022, a group of men flew to Los Angeles with funds provided by Durk, followed Rondo and his crew around, and three gunmen fired on his Escalade near the Beverly Center shopping mall in Los Angeles. Rondo survived, but his 24-year-old cousin, Saviay’a Robinson, known as Lul Pab, was killed.

“Today, the jury delivered justice to the family of Saviay’a Robinson, finding defendants Deandre Wilson and David Lindsey guilty of stalking resulting in Mr. Robinson’s death,” First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said in a statement. “While we are disappointed with the jury’s decision regarding Durk Banks, a.k.a. ‘Lil Durk,’ we look forward to presenting our evidence at his second trial.”

Durk won a Grammy earlier that year for Best Melodic Rap Performance for “All My Life,” which features J. Cole. He has been nominated for three other Grammys and was a featured performer on Drake’s “Laugh Now Cry Later.” /ra

articles.title: UAAP: UP title redemption bid gets boost with Veejay Pre in tow
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines—The University of the Philippines finally gets to parade crack center Veejay Pre in the upcoming UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball tournament. After serving his residency last year,…

blocks.text: FILE- Big man Veejay Pre reacts during a game against UST in UAAP Season 87.–MARLO CUETO/INQUIRER.net
MANILA, Philippines—The University of the Philippines finally gets to parade crack center Veejay Pre in the upcoming UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball tournament.

After serving his residency last year, Pre will be making his much-awaited debut for the Fighting Maroons, looking to pick up where he left off following a promising one-and-done stint with Far Eastern University.
UP assistant coach Christian Luanzon is confident Pre will make instant impact for the Maroons, who finished second to La Salle last season.
“Veejay has been in the UAAP for the longest time since he was in high school and when he came in with us, he had a year to adjust,” Luanzon said.
“He’s hardworking, he always has an open mind, not just with his coaches but also with his teammates.”

In his only season in Morayta, where he was named UAAP Rookie of the Year averaging 13.2 and 7 rebounds, Pre established himself as the future not just in the UAAP but Philippine basketball in general.
He then transferred to Diliman, where he will be a key piece of UP’s title redemption bid.
“Whenever someone new enters the team, we impart our culture to them so there’s always an adjustment.”
“But, even as an established player of the league, having won Rookie of the Year before, he listens to advice. He’s always all ears and looking for room to grow.”
Pre makes his UP debut on Sunday against University of Santo Tomas to cap off an opening tripleheader at Araneta Coliseum.

articles.title: Sibonga farmer, 60, gunned down aboard motorbike to fiesta
articles.summary: A 60-year-old farmer was shot dead by unidentified motorcycle-riding suspects in Purok 3, Barangay Can-aga, Sibonga, Cebu, on Friday afternoon, Sept. 11, 2026.... Keep on reading: Sibonga farmer, 60,…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY, Philippines — A 60-year-old farmer was shot dead by unidentified motorcycle-riding suspects in Purok 3, Barangay Can-aga, Sibonga, Cebu, on Friday afternoon, Sept. 11, 2026.
Police identified the victim as Domingo, a resident of Purok 5 in the same barangay.
According to the initial investigation by the Sibonga Municipal Police Station, the incident took place at around 1:10 p.m.
Domingo was riding his motorcycle from home to Barangay Cantularoy to attend a fiesta.
As he reached Purok 3, he was waylaid and shot multiple times by the unidentified gunmen, resulting in his death.
Responding police personnel arrived at the crime scene shortly after, around 1:30 p.m.
The victim’s 40-year-old child recalled being at a deep well near the barangay road—approximately two kilometers from their residence—bathing when the incident occurred.
Riding in tandem
The witness spotted two men riding a white-and-black motorcycle, both wearing black jackets, jeans, and black sunglasses.
Just moments after the suspects passed, consecutive gunshots echoed from a few meters away.

Upon checking the area, the witness was met with the horrifying sight of Domingo lying lifeless in the middle of the road beside his motorcycle. The victim bore multiple gunshot wounds across his body.
Authorities are conducting a follow-up investigation to identify the suspects, track down their whereabouts, and determine the motive behind the fatal attack.
Police urge anyone with relevant information regarding the suspects or the incident to come forward to help bring justice to the victim and his grieving family.

articles.title: Comelec removes with finality Moro Ako Party from BARMM 2026 poll roster
articles.summary: The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has ruled with finality on the disqualification of the Moro Ako Party from the Major Regional Parliamentary Political Party (RPPP) roster for the upcoming BARMM…

blocks.text: Published September 12, 2026 6:31pm

The Commission on Elections (Comelec) has ruled with finality on the disqualification of the Moro Ako Party from the Major Regional Parliamentary Political Party (RPPP) roster for the upcoming BARMM parliamentary elections.

In a Certificate of Finality and Entry of Judgment dated September 7, 2026, the Commission said it did not receive a motion for reconsideration on the en banc ruling that affirmed Moro Ako's disqualification.

The motion could have been filed within five days of the party's receipt of the August 27 resolution of the Commission en Banc, with the intent to preclude the order from being final and executory, according to the document which was made public on Saturday.
In the August 27 ruling, the Commission En Banc affirmed its decision to deny the appeal of Moro Ako Party for "lack of merit."

The poll body dismissed Moro Ako's appeal regarding the cancellation of its registration and accreditation as an RPPP after the party failed to satisfy registration requirements and allegedly committed material misrepresentation.
Under Comelec Resolution 11271, the cancellation of Moro Ako Party's registration and accreditation is considered final and executory.

"Its accreditation as a Major RPPP is deemed revoked, and all entitlements, privileges, and preferences granted to it, including the allotment of the 12th copy of the election returns and the privilege to appoint watchers, are hereby withdrawn," it added.

articles.title: Cesafi Season 26: Magis Eagles outlast Baby Lancers in season opener
articles.summary: The five-peat defending champions Sacred Heart School-Ateneo de Cebu (SHS-AdC) Magis Eagles opened their title-retention campaign with a hard-fought 61-56 victory over the University of the Visayas…

blocks.text: TAGBILARAN CITY, Philippines — The five-peat defending champions Sacred Heart School-Ateneo de Cebu (SHS-AdC) Magis Eagles opened their title-retention campaign with a hard-fought 61-56 victory over the University of the Visayas (UV) Baby Lancers in the Cebu Schools Athletic Foundation, Inc. (Cesafi) Season 26 high school basketball tournament at the Cebu Coliseum.
Seeking a sixth straight title, the Magis Eagles were immediately tested by a tough and gritty Baby Lancers squad now coached by veteran mentor Raymond Mercader.
But SHS-AdC’s championship pedigree was on full display as the defending champions weathered UV’s challenge.
Gilas Pilipinas Youth selection and SHS-AdC’s new main big man Jibson Gaviola led the Magis Eagles with 14 points, seven rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block.
Last season’s MVP and fellow Gilas Pilipinas Youth cager Lian Kent Basa added 11 points, five rebounds, three assists, three steals and one block.
Johnrey Recio and Jacob Javelosa chipped in 10 points apiece for the Magis Eagles.
Kirbey Borbon paced UV with a game-high 18 points, along with three rebounds, one assist, one steal and one block.
Dominant performance
The Magis Eagles dominated inside, outscoring UV, 42-30, in the paint. The Baby Lancers, however, had the edge in bench production, 36-24.

UV refused to let the defending champions pull away, preventing SHS-AdC from building a double-digit lead. The Baby Lancers also forced seven lead changes and three ties in a game many expected to be a lopsided season-opening victory for the defending champions.
In the other game, the University of Cebu Lapu-Lapu and Mandaue (UCLM) Junior Webmasters dominated the Benedicto College (BC) Baby Cheetahs, 69-43, behind a 22-point eruption from Klent Ovillo.

Ovillo made an impressive Cesafi debut, shooting 9-of-12 from the field while adding five rebounds, two steals and one assist. Carl Torreon contributed 15 points as UCLM improved to 2-0, while handing the Baby Cheetahs their second straight loss to open the season.
Axel Joseph Oropisa and Andre Patino led BC with 16 and 12 points, respectively, in the losing effort.
UCLM established control early, taking a commanding 38-20 lead at halftime. The Junior Webmasters continued to pull away in the second half and led by as many as 28 points.
