articles.title: Hijacking pirates exploit regional chaos to return to seas off Somalia
articles.summary:
US-Israel war on Iran and political instability in Somalia lead to pirates targeting cargo ships off Horn of Africa

The scourge of Somali piracy targeting cargo ships and smaller dhows off…
articles.byline: Mohamed Gabobe in Mogadishu and Peter Beaumont

blocks.text: The scourge of Somali piracy targeting cargo ships and smaller dhows off the Horn of Africa has returned to levels not seen in a decade, driven by a convergence of factors including disruptions to the shipping industry caused by the US-Israeli war against Iran and a resurgence of political instability in Somalia.

Since late April there have been eight hijackings by Somali pirates, including two within the space of a fortnight in August: one targeting an oil tanker with ties to Iran, the other a Cameroon-flagged vessel, the Lutuf, carrying military equipment for Turkey.

Over a seven-year period from 2005 there were more than 1,000 attacks on vessels in the waters off Somalia, which has Africa’s longest coastline. Thousands of crew members were taken hostage, netting $400m (£296m) in ransom payments for the piracy network’s financiers, the low-level “foot-soldier” pirates and the communities who provided them with goods and services. The attacks only petered out after a multinational anti-piracy force was deployed.

blocks.caption: Armed Somali pirates guard the beach in Hobyo district, 540km north-east of Mogadishu, in 2008.  Photograph: Badri Media/epa/Corbis

blocks.text: The hijacking of the Lutuf was the most high-profile of the recent incidents. Turkey has been expanding its influence in Somalia after an agreement signed in 2024 to build up its navy, and the Lutuf’s release two weeks after its capture involved a joint Turkish-Somali operation that resulted in the destruction of four pirate vessels.

However, local officials including Mohamed Mubarak, the head of the Puntland security coordination office, have said that a $2.5m (£1.85m) ransom was also paid, prompting warnings that such payments risked encouraging similar incidents.

blocks.caption: Members of Somalia Puntland maritime police force on duty in 2023.  Photograph: Daniel Irungu/EPA

blocks.text: In a comment for the Center for Maritime Security in July, Matthew Reisener, the thinktank’s national security adviser, warned that naval campaigns by Iran in the strait of Hormuz and Iran’s Houthi proxies in the Red Sea – launched in response to the US-Israel war on Iran – are allowing regional piracy “to once again thrive”.

He wrote: “Not only have the global navies that once combatted piracy off the Horn of Africa diverted their resources to counter the threats against ships in these critical waterways, but these conflicts have also drawn maritime traffic closer to Somalia’s coastline, creating openings for opportunistic pirates to target commercial ships.”
According to Reisener, about 70% of maritime traffic that passed through the Red Sea prior to the Houthis’ targeting of ships there is now being rerouted around the Cape of Good Hope in South Africa.

A report by the International Institute for Strategic Studies in May reached a similar conclusion: “The recent deterioration of maritime security followed a prolonged period of relative calm in the waters off the Somali coast, which resulted in the redeployment of international anti-piracy fleets and the relaxation of commercial risk-management practices. These factors – alongside the distraction posed by Houthi attacks in the Red Sea – have converged to create an opening that Somali pirates have been quick to exploit.”
Analysts also note that rising oil prices driven by the war have made oil cargoes a more valuable target.

Among the least developed countries in the world, Somalia has endured conflict and clan battles with no strong central government since the autocratic ruler Mohamed Siad Barre fell in 1991. Insufficient patrol vessels and an inability to regularly pay salaries to those involved in coastal patrols are among the reasons why Somalia has long-struggled to secure its coastline.

blocks.caption: Yemenis protest against Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping. Experts warn that these attacks in response to the US-Israel war on Iran are allowing piracy to thrive. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty

blocks.text: Piracy has historically thrived during periods of increasing instability and political, factional and regional competition. Observers say the recent rise in incidents has been exacerbated by a domestic and international focus on arms smuggling to Yemen by networks acting on behalf of Iran. Analysts suggest some of these networks have become increasingly associated with Somalia’s Islamist al-Shabaab group as it once again expands its territorial control in central and southern Somalia and seeks to build ties with the Houthis in Yemen.
Local officials interviewed by the Guardian described how in the recent spate of incidents, pirate groups have been using vessels they had already seized to attack and capture other vessels.

According to the officials, the Lutuf was approached as it sailed three nautical miles from Somali shores near the fishing town of Maraya by a previously hijacked cement carrier, the MV Sward, which had been repurposed as a pirate mothership. Eight gunmen from the Sward then boarded the Lutuf and were able to overpower the ship’s armed guards.

blocks.caption: The MV Sward, a cement carrier hijacked in April, was repurposed as a pirate mothership. Photograph: EU Naval Force Operation Atalanta

blocks.text: Officials say the recent attacks have also been marked by increased technological sophistication on the part of pirate groups, including the use of SpaceX’s Starlink satellite internet service to facilitate the tracking of potential targets and for high-speed communications between pirates.

That reflects what Lloyd’s List has described as an increasingly “more capable and adaptive Somali piracy threat” that is already exposing vulnerabilities in carriers’ existing anti-piracy security measures.

In the weeks since the Lutuf ransom was paid, residents of Galkayo, a commercial hub in the north-central Mudug region, said money had started circulating through the local economy to a much greater degree than before. Consumption of the stimulant khat has reportedly increased, and greater numbers of expensive sports utility vehicles have been seen on the roads.

blocks.caption: Residents of Galkayo, Somalia, said money has begun to circulate in the local economy since the hijacking of the Lutuf. Photograph: Gary Calton/The Observer

blocks.text: During the previous piracy boom, increased flows of money through the economies of coastal communities and places like Galkayo had profound societal impacts, including an expansion of alcohol and drug use and prostitution.

Perhaps foreshadowing the regime of tougher measures that may be required to counter the growing piracy threat, the Lutuf was only released after a series of drone attacks on the pirate groups involved in the seizure, both at sea and on land. The dead included nine armed men who were killed by a missile fired from a Turkish drone as they prepared boats to join the gunmen onboard the Lutuf.
The question now is whether the growing threat can be countered.

Writing in The Conversation in May, the UK-based academics Anja Shortland and Federico Varese, who studied Somalia’s piracy problem in 2014, were uncertain whether there was an international appetite or the capacity for the same sort of anti-piracy force deployed more than a decade ago.

blocks.caption: Somali pirates apprehended by French soldiers in the Gulf of Aden in 2009. Photograph: Sipa Press/Rex Features

blocks.text: “What happens next will depend on how the current hijacks proceed. Pirates rely on ransoms for reinvestment and to attract young men into their no-win-no-fee contracts. Fast and generous payments … may free the captive ships. But they will lead to escalating risks for everyone else.

“No state or alliance also currently has the will or capacity to run a naval mission on the scale seen in 2011 and 2012, when navies worldwide spent more than US$1bn annually on counter-piracy operations off Somalia.
“Although piracy manifests as a sea-based problem, it can only be solved on land.”

articles.title: Nepal says big polluters must ‘wake up’ as it calls for climate compensation over flood disaster
articles.summary:
Foreign minister Shisir Khanal tells the Guardian the world’s biggest economies need to help Nepal, which contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions

Nepal is demanding…

blocks.text: Nepal is demanding $20m in climate compensation for the recent devastating floods, as a senior minister called on the world’s most polluting countries to “wake up” and accept shared responsibility for a disaster that led to the death or disappearance of more than 6,000 people.

Scientists believe the climate crisis had a role to play in the floods, which were triggered when a melting glacier partially collapsed and set off a deadly landslide and flash flooding through Chinese-controlled Tibet and Nepal in late August. So far, more than 1,300 are confirmed dead and more than 5,500 still missing, with hopes of their survival diminished after 12 days of rescue operations.

Speaking to the Guardian, Nepal’s foreign minister, Shisir Khanal, was forthright in his call for climate justice and said it was imperative the world’s biggest economies stepped up to help Nepal recover and rebuild after the catastrophic floods.

Nepal contributes less than 0.1% of global greenhouse gas emissions, while its neighbours India and China are among the world’s biggest emitters. The mountains of the Himalayas – which span across India, China, Nepal and Bhutan – have been warming at a rate nearly 50% faster than the global average.
In 2023, the UN said Nepal’s mountains had lost close to a third of their ice in just over 30 years due to global heating.

Khanal emphasised that the recent disaster was far more extreme than any flooding regularly seen during the monsoon season, and said the magnitude of damage was on par with the 2015 earthquake that left much of the country in ruins.

blocks.caption: An excavator repairs a damaged road in Nepal near the Trishuli River on Monday. Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

blocks.text: “This felt like a tsunami that was coming from the Himalayas,” he said. “We experienced waves as high as 60, 70 feet, which were mixed with debris, mud, stones, rocks, and came at the speed of almost 180km per hour. Towns, villages and highways were completely wiped out and there are some areas still disconnected.”

Khanal confirmed that Nepal’s ministry of finance and ministry of environment had written a joint letter to the UN’s fund for responding to loss and damage – which was set up in 2022 in line with the Paris climate agreement – to request $20m in climate-related damages.

“We have contributed so little to climate change,” he said. “It is imperative for those in the global community who benefit from larger, much more polluting economies, and whose historical contribution to greenhouse gases is much bigger than ours, to accept a shared responsibility. This affects all of humanity.”
For Nepal, the disaster was particularly worrying because it was “one of the strongest warning signals that we’ve experienced of what’s to come”, he said.

“The global community should not see this as one-off disaster; it should be viewed in the context of the changing climate in the Himalayas,” he said. “We know it is going to be a recurring scenario that more and more communities, not just in Nepal but around the world, will have to face.”

Khanal acknowledged that the compensation amount Nepal has requested from the UN was “obviously not nearly enough to cover the damage that we have sustained”. According to some estimates, the total damage caused by the floods will be upwards of $5bn, though Khanal said it could be even higher.

Upwards of 20,000 homes will probably have to be rebuilt, as well as the main highway. Villages built in vulnerable areas along the river, some of which washed away entirely, may have to be relocated to higher, safer ground.

While Khanal initially singled out India and China as countries that should step in to help – while avoiding mention of the US, which is the world’s biggest polluter – he rowed back on those comments, saying: “It is not just about shifting the blame to one or the other country, it’s about us all working together.”

blocks.caption: Damaged buildings on the banks of the Trishuli River. Photograph: Anushree Fadnavis/Reuters

blocks.text: He emphasised that the compensation demand was also meant to act as a “wake-up call for the global community to establish a more robust mechanism to help vulnerable and small economies like Nepal”.

The UN has admitted the loss and damage fund is already facing a “significant financing gap”. The fund has already received requests totalling $2.8bn from about 119 countries, but so far only around $400m has been given by the international community. The US has given just $17m, after Donald Trump withdrew from the Paris agreement.
Khanal acknowledged there were “political challenges” in getting Nepal the climate compensation it was demanding.
“Yes there always will be people who may not agree to our perspective or deny there is climate change, but there are also people who deny that the Earth is round,” he said bluntly.
He emphasised the importance of funds being made available not just for immediate disaster response but also for preparedness and mitigation for climate-related risk.

Khanal rebuffed allegations that China had failed to give an adequate warning or share data with Nepal about the impending floods. He said he was in discussion with China about enhancing coordination and data sharing for the Himalayan region.
“With the benefit of hindsight, we can now see that this glacier was fragile and had been receding in the past six months,” he said.

“But before the floods hit, there was no knowledge on our part, or on the part of Chinese scientists, that this particular collapse was imminent. I do not believe any of us had any idea of the threat until it happened.”

articles.title: Water levels at San Roque Dam, Pangasinan rivers remain under close watch
articles.summary: PANGASINAN---San Roque dam continued to release water Monday morning as several rivers in Pangasinan remained above normal levels, including one that remained above the critical level. As of 5 a.m.…

blocks.text: (Photo via Liezle Inigo)
PANGASINAN---San Roque dam continued to release water Monday morning as several rivers in Pangasinan remained above normal levels, including one that remained above the critical level.
As of 5 a.m. on Sept. 7, the dam’s water level was at 279.79 meters above sea level (masl), with an inflow of 338 cubic meters per second (cms) and a combined outflow of 746 cms.
Two gates were opened at the dam. Gate No. 2A was opened to 1.0 meter, while Gate No. 2B was opened to 1.5 meters. The Low Level Outlet was also releasing 125 cms.
The elevated discharge comes as authorities continue to monitor river conditions downstream, particularly communities located near waterways and flood-prone areas.

At 6 a.m., the Marusay River in Calasiao was above the critical level, while the Sinucalan River in Sta. Barbara, Pantal River in Dagupan City, and Agno/Bañaga River in Bugallon were above normal levels.
The Camiling River in Camiling, Tarlac was at normal level. No level reading was indicated in the monitoring report for the Bued/Cayanga River in San Fabian and Balingcaguing River in Mabini.
Residents near rivers and low-lying communities are urged to remain alert, monitor advisories, and follow evacuation or other safety directives when issued.

articles.title: 'Takot yan?': VP Duterte doesn't talk, act like someone who is in fear, says Adiong
articles.summary: House Assistant Majority Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong says Vice President Sara Duterte doesn't appear to be fearing for her life, as she has claimed, based on her known demeanor.…

blocks.text: House Assistant Majority Lanao del Sur 1st district Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong says Vice President Sara Duterte doesn't appear to be fearing for her life, as she has claimed, based on her known demeanor.

This, as Adiong chided Duterte for playing the victim card after being issued an arrest warrant for three counts of grave threats, which stemmed from claims of planning to assassinate President Marcos and other members of the First Family.
The Vice President’s ordeal prompted her to declare over the weekend, "I do not feel safe. Pakiramdam ko papatayin nila [pulis] ako (I feel the police is out to kill me).
"I have documented threats and harrassment since 2023. I fear for my children. I do not feel they are safe if I am with them," she also said.
But Adiong doesn't buy Duterte’s fearful facade one bit.
“Kung titignan niyo, hindi po ito yung taong takot (If you look at her, she does not appear to be someone who is afraid). Actually, in fact, it’s the other way around,” he said.

He also pointed to Duterte’s previous public statements that he said appeared to invoke violence against President Marcos, as well as her continued requests for travel clearance, as inconsistent with her claim that she had been under threat since 2023.

“Siya yung nagbibigay ng mga statement na nagpapahiwatig ng violence against the President, pupugutan ng ulo (She was the one making statements suggesting violence against the President, including that he would be beheaded)... So it’s not an indication of someone who’s been receiving threats,” he said.
These notwithstanding, Adiong stressed that any threat against Duterte should be taken seriously and properly investigated by authorities.
He said the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) had given her an opportunity to submit information about the threats she claimed to have received, but no such information had been provided.

“They were given the chance. They were called, invited by the NBI na isubmit po nila kung ano po yung threats na ... natatanggap nila (They were called and invited by the NBI to submit information about the threats they had received.
“Pero hanggang ngayon, wala po silang naibibigay (But until now, they have not provided anything)," Adiong noted.

Seemingly referring to Duterte’s subsequent criticisms on the court and police, the Mindanao congressman stressed that public officials should respect the courts and the law even when proceedings or their outcomes are unfavorable to them.

“In this case, whether or not favorable sa’yo, kailangan mo talaga as an elected official to prove to the people that we have our laws, we have to respect our laws, and only through our laws and through our courts can we defend ourselves."

(In this case, whether or not it is favorable to you, as an elected official you have to prove to the people that we have laws, that we have to respect them, and that only through our laws and courts can we defend ourselves.)
The law applies to everyone

For Adiong, the grave threats case demonstrates that the law applies equally to everyone regardless of status or position, rejecting claims from Duterte’s camp and supporters that the proceedings constitute political persecution.

“Ito pong nangyayari ngayon, ito po ang nagpapatunay na gumugulong po ang hustisya sa ating bansa. Wala pong tinitingnan na status or posisyon ng isang tao pagdating sa pananagutan at sa pag-implement ng mga patakaran o ating batas,” he said.

(What is happening now proves that justice is taking its course in our country. No one’s status or position is considered when it comes to accountability and the implementation of our rules and laws.)
He said the criminal case should also be distinguished from Duterte’s ongoing impeachment proceedings.
“Magkaiba naman po yung mga hukom na tumatayo dito at yung magiging verdict po ay magkaiba (The judges handling these cases are different, and the verdicts will also be different)."

articles.title: DSWD flags bogus UPLIFT aid for students
articles.summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Sept. 7, flagged social media posts offering supposed educational assistance to students under the Unified Package for Livelihood,…

blocks.text: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) on Monday, Sept. 7, flagged social media posts offering supposed educational assistance to students under the Unified Package for Livelihood, Industry, Food, and Transport (UPLIFT) Assistance.

The posts claim that the government is giving ₱2,000 to elementary students, ₱3,000 to junior high school students, ₱5,000 to senior high school students, and ₱8,000 to college students under the program.
DSWD Assistant Secretary and spokesperson Irene Dumlao said educational assistance is not part of UPLIFT.

“Paalala po natin sa ating mga kababayan na walang educational assistance sa ilalim po ng ating UPLIFT Assistance. Ito pong assistance na ito ay tulong maibsan ang epekto ng pagtaas ng presyo ng mga bilihin (We remind our fellow Filipinos that there is no educational assistance under UPLIFT Assistance. This assistance is intended to help ease the impact of rising prices of goods),” Dumlao said.
The posts also direct users to registration links, which the DSWD said are unauthorized.
Dumlao said there is no need to register for UPLIFT because its beneficiaries have already been identified using the latest Community-Based Monitoring System (CBMS) data.

“Mangyaring huwag po i-click ang inyong mga makikitang link na nagsasabing maaari kayong magparehistro dahil scam po ito (Please do not click on links claiming that you can register because these are scams),” she added.
Qualified beneficiaries under Groups 2 and 3 of the UPLIFT program receive ₱2,000 per month until December.

UPLIFT Assistance is among the Marcos administration’s initiatives to help poor, near-poor, and low-income Filipinos cope with the economic impact of the energy emergency brought about by the geopolitical conflict in the Middle East.
The public may verify information on UPLIFT Assistance and other DSWD programs through the Department’s official social media pages or the DSWD Online Grievance Portal.

articles.title: Alcantara, partner rule doubles tilt in Thailand
articles.summary: Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the…

blocks.text: At A Glance

items: Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the ITF M15 Nonthaburi in Thailand over the weekend.

blocks.text: (Francis Casey Alcantara / Facebook / Impact )

Francis Casey Alcantara and Thai Pawit Sornlaksup displayed nerves of steel and hacked out a 7-6 (4), 5-7, 10-8 victory over Indian pair Manish Sureshkumar and Maan Kesharwani to reign supreme in the ITF M15 Nonthaburi in Thailand over the weekend.
Alcantara, 34, and Sornlaksup recovered from a second-set stumble and held their ground by protecting their 8-3 advantage to fend of their persistent Indian rivals.
“Thank you Pawit Sornlaksup for an incredible week and for carrying me through some tough matches!” Alcantara wrote on social media.
“It was a pleasure sharing the court with you bro! Special thanks to Coach Coach Carlo Core Tennis Academy BKK for always being there and helping me out again this week,” he added.
Prior to their title victory, Alcantara and Sornlaksup outlasted locals Thantub Suksumrarn and Tanapatt Nirundorn (7-5, 7-5) in the opening round.

They followed it up with a gritty 6-2, 4-6, 11-9 quarters victory over Japanese Shu Muto and Ko Suzuki to book their ticket to the semifinals, where they ultimately pulled off a 1-6, 6-4, 10-4 triumph against Americans Hugo Hashimoto and Michael Blando.
The tournament serves as a training ground for Alcantara, who will be competing in the 20th Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 late this month.

articles.title: Ely Buendia, Chito Miranda sell out Dubai concert amid Middle East tensions
articles.summary: Ongoing tensions across the Middle East have cast a shadow over the region’s live entertainment business, with uncertainty surrounding travel, consumer spending and large-scale public events making…

blocks.text: Ongoing tensions across the Middle East have cast a shadow over the region’s live entertainment business, with uncertainty surrounding travel, consumer spending and large-scale public events making concert planning a more complicated proposition.
And yet, some acts continue to defy the odds, demonstrating that music can be more than entertainment in uncertain times.
Ely Buendia and Chito Miranda were among those artists
The two brought OPM nostalgia to Dubai on Aug. 30, performing to a sold-out Coca-Cola Arena.
For the UAE’s Filipino community, the show also offered something beyond nostalgia: a chance to reconnect with home through live music at a time when the region remains unsettled.

Buendia, best known as the former frontman of Eraserheads, and Miranda, lead vocalist of Parokya ni Edgar, represent different eras of Philippine rock but share a deep connection with Filipino audiences.
The concert was presented by Tiana Entertainment Inc., headed by founder and CEO Bojie Yangco, who has worked in live entertainment for more than two decades.

The company has mounted Filipino concerts in markets including the U.S., Canada, Australia, the Middle East and Kazakhstan, with artists such as Rivermaya, SB19, Ben&Ben, Buendia and Miranda among its previous projects.

articles.title: Palace respects Ombudsman filing of plunder case vs Romualdez
articles.summary: Malacañang said it respects the Office of the Ombudsman’s decision to file a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, President Marcos’ cousin, over his alleged involvement in the…

blocks.text: Malacañang said it respects the Office of the Ombudsman’s decision to file a plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez, President Marcos’ cousin, over his alleged involvement in the flood control scandal. In a press briefing on Monday, Sept. 7, Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the Palace respects the Ombudsman’s decision as it is only performing its duties. “Iginagalang po natin ang aksyon ng Ombudsman dahil ito naman po ay nasa kanilang mandato (We respect the action of the Ombudsman because this is within its mandate),” she said. While the Palace had yet to receive a formal statement from President Marcos on the development, Castro said the President had already made clear his position on accountability. “Ang sa Pangulo naman po ay kung sino po ang dapat managot ay dapat na panagutin (The President’s position is that whoever should be held accountable should be held accountable),” she said. “Kung sino man po 'yan — kamag-anak, kaibigan, kaalyado, o kalaban sa pulitika (Whoever that may be — a relative, a friend, an ally, or a political opponent),” she added. Castro said the evidence should determine the course of the case, while those charged would have the opportunity to defend themselves. “Kung ano po ang isinisigaw ng ebidensya, dapat lamang po itong mailahad (Whatever the evidence shows, it should be brought to light),” she said. “Depende na po 'yan sa mga makakasuhan kung sila man po ay may sapat na ebidensya para ipaglaban ang kanilang sarili, nasa kanila na po 'yan (It will then be up to those charged, if they have sufficient evidence to defend themselves, to do so),” she added. Asked whether Marcos had expressed personal feelings about the case involving his cousin, Castro said she had not asked the President about it, but recalled his remarks during his fifth State of the Nation Address in July that he was prepared to let the evidence guide the government’s actions. “‘Pag ebidensya ang nagsusumigaw, kailangan po itong malaman ng taumbayan (When the evidence speaks, the people need to know about it),” she said. The Ombudsman filed the plunder case before the Sandiganbayan on Monday, accusing Romualdez and former Ako Bicol Rep. Zaldy Co of allegedly committing “concerted and coordinated acts” to unlawfully amass about P56 billion in ill-gotten wealth from 2022 to 2025. Romualdez has repeatedly denied involvement in the alleged flood control anomalies and has said he is ready to face the charges and prove his side, while his legal team has questioned the evidence against him. The filing follows Marcos’ July SONA disclosure that the Ombudsman was preparing criminal cases against his cousin. “Masakit man sa akin ito, pero kailangan nating gawin ang tama (Painful as this may be for me, but we have to do what is right),” the President said. “Hindi ako pangulo ng aking pamilya. Hindi ako pangulo ng aking kaibigan. Ako ay Pangulo ng Pilipinas at ang tungkulin ko ay sa inyo, ang aking mga kapwa Pilipino (I am not the president of my family. I am not the president of my friends. I am the President of the Philippines, and my duty is to you, my fellow Filipinos),” he added.

articles.title: Former UK PM Cameron keynotes 27th World Knowledge Forum
articles.summary: SEOUL - Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom David Cameron will lead the opening of the 27th World Knowledge Forum (WKF) today, Sept. 8, at the Jangchung Arena here under the theme "The…

blocks.text: SEOUL - Former Prime Minister of the United Kingdom David Cameron will lead the opening of the 27th World Knowledge Forum (WKF) today, Sept. 8, at the Jangchung Arena here under the theme "The Promethean Moment: Architecting the Co-Intelligence Order."

Against the backdrop of profound discussions on the thoughtful coexistence of humanity and Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cameron, the 75th Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, will deliver his keynote address on "A New Order of Co-intelligence in the Age of AI."
Cameron is expected to draw from his experience in reviving the British economy through deregulatory and structural reforms following the 2008 global financial crisis.
He will offer strategic insights on the leadership required to navigate today's compounding crises defined by the AI revolution and heightened geopolitical uncertainty.

Also joining the roster of speakers in this year’s iteration of the WKF are Go Negosyo founder and Association of Southeast Asian Nations-Business Advisory Council (ASEAN-BAC) Chairman Jose Ma. Concepcion III who will also receive the ASEAN Entrepreneurs Award together with Don Lam, CEO of VinaCapital.

Other speakers are Cho Jung-sik, Speaker of the National Assembly, former Prime Minister of Denmark Helle Thorning-Schmidt, former Japanese Prime Minister Ishiba Shigeru, and former New York City Mayor Eric Adams.
This year's forum will bring together close to 70,000 participants and 6,303 world-renowned speakers from 86 countries to share fresh insights for humanity as we enter the era of AI.

Dr. Chang Dae-whan, WKF founder and chairman of the Maekyung Media, said the 27th World Knowledge Forum is being held at a critical juncture, as the established order driving global economic growth collapses and protectionism and geopolitical tensions intensify.
“Confronting low growth and unexpected leadership changes, South Korea urgently requires comprehensive innovation and bold challenges across all sectors.”
“In particular, rapid technological advancements led by AI are reshaping industry and politics, throwing humanity into a sweeping transformation,” Chang said.

He added that while major powers invest astronomical sums in technologies like semiconductors, quantum computing, and robotics, concerns are mounting over winner-takes-all monopolies and job displacement, further intensifying social conflicts.
To break through these simultaneous crises, Chang said Maeil Business Newspaper chose this year's main theme: “The Promethean Moment: Architecting the Co-Intelligence Order.”

“The mythical ‘Promethean Moment’ signifies a historical turning point when humanity received ' fire '—a revolutionary tool that drove civilization forward, yet acted as a double-edged sword if left uncontrolled,” he said.
“Likewise, we hope humanity can overcome this civilizational upheaval brought by AI with wisdom, ultimately architecting a new order where technology and humanity coexist,” Chang added.

Prominent speakers at previous WKFs have included state leaders such as George W. Bush, the 43rd President of the United States; Theresa May, the 76th Prime Minister of the United Kingdom; Nicolas Sarkozy, the 23rd President of the French Republic; and Gerhard Schrfder, the 7th Chancellor of Germany. Presidents of international organizations have also participated, including Jim Yong Kim, the 12th President of the World Bank. Founders and CEOs such as Bill Gates, Co-founder of Microsoft Corporation; Larry Ellison, Chairman and CEO of Oracle Corporation; John L. Hennessy, Chairman of Alphabet; and George Soros, Chairman of Soros Fund Management, have graced the forum. Scholars including Larry Summers, Paul Krugman, Michael Porter, and Gregory Mankiw have also addressed the forum.

articles.title: Jhonny Bobier breaks silence on ‘Tatsulok’ controversy, says he was ‘intentionally humiliated’
articles.summary: Filmmaker Jhonny Bobier has finally spoken up about the controversy surrounding his film “Tatsulok,” saying he felt he was deliberately put in an embarrassing situation over allegations that he…

blocks.text: Filmmaker Jhonny Bobier has finally spoken up about the controversy surrounding his film “Tatsulok,” saying he felt he was deliberately put in an embarrassing situation over allegations that he screened it publicly using fake MTRCB permit. In a video statement sent to GMA News Online, Bobier denied having anything to do with the alleged falsified Permit to Exhibit (PTE) linked to “Tatsulok Trilogy” and Tanajuan Pelikula Production. “I had nothing to do with that alleged fake MTRCB permit. I do not know where it came from,” Bobier said, as quoted by GMA News Online. The Movie and Television Review and Classification Board (MTRCB) earlier said “Tatsulok” had not undergone its review and classification process and had no valid PTE. The agency also said it discovered a fake permit connected to the film and its production company. Bobier, however, maintained that he never obtained an MTRCB permit for the film’s August 21 premiere. According to his account, this was his first time independently handling the requirements for a public film screening, after previously having such matters handled through film festivals. He said he relied on a Gateway Cineplex representative who handled the agreement for the screening and believed the cinema would inform him about the necessary requirements. Bobier also claimed he understood that a permit was needed for the planned August 29 public screening, not the August 21 premiere. The situation came to a head during the premiere when a cinema representative allegedly asked him for an MTRCB permit and warned that the screening could be stopped without one. Bobier said he decided to proceed with the event because the venue had already been paid for and guests were already waiting to watch the film. It was the timing of the issue that particularly troubled him. The director described the cinema management's decision to raise the permit concern at the last minute as suspicious, arguing that he should have been informed earlier if the document was a requirement. More importantly, Bobier said the incident left him feeling deliberately embarrassed in front of the people who had supported his film. “I cannot help but feel that they tried to humiliate me and embarrass me in front of those people who supported my film,” Bobier said. He further described the experience as being “intentionally cornered and humiliated,” saying it made him appear irresponsible for an administrative issue he claimed he did not create or know about. The filmmaker's comments come after Gateway Cineplex 18 issued a public notice on August 26 saying it was not associated with Tanajuan Pelikula or the planned August 29 screening of “Tatsulok.” The cinema also said the film would not be shown at any of its cinemas. Bobier said the notice prompted him to finally give his own account of what happened. He is now working with his lawyer and is seeking due process as the controversy continues.

articles.title: Government calamity spending surges 35% at end-August as disasters strike
articles.summary: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction…

blocks.text: Amid recent calamities, government disaster spending has accelerated rapidly, with total releases from the calamity fund climbing to ₱14 billion at end-August to support response and reconstruction requirements nationwide.

Data from the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) showed that cumulative end-August releases jumped by 35.3 percent from the end-July total of ₱10.4 billion. As of Aug. 31, the available balance of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Fund (NDRRMF) stood at ₱26.1 billion.

This total is drawn from a ₱40.2 billion budget for fiscal year 2026—consisting of ₱23.5 billion for the NDRRM Program (NDRRMP), ₱15.3 billion for the Disaster Rehabilitation and Reconstruction Assistance Program (DRRAP) for local government units, and ₱1 billion for the People’s Survival Fund (PSF)—supplemented by ₱322.9 million in continuing appropriations from 2025.

To date, all disbursements have been sourced exclusively from the NDRRMP. The bulk, totaling ₱12.9 billion, was directed toward Quick Response Fund (QRF) augmentations for immediate relief and rehabilitation. Meanwhile, ₱1.1 billion was released for specific rehabilitation and logistics projects approved by the Office of the President (OP).
While the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) was previously the sole recipient of QRF augmentations, several other national agencies have now received standby funds.

The DSWD remains the largest recipient, drawing ₱11.4 billion in total QRF replenishments across six tranches: ₱2 billion in February, ₱1.9 billion in March, ₱2 billion in April, ₱1.7 billion in June, ₱2 billion in July, and ₱1.8 billion in August.
Among other agencies receiving emergency funds, the Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) received ₱1.2 billion in August for its first QRF replenishment of the year.

The Department of National Defense (DND) received ₱300 million in July for the Office of Civil Defense (OCD) QRF, while the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) received ₱50 million in July for the Philippine National Police (PNP) QRF.

Apart from emergency relief, the ₱1.1 billion approved by the OP for targeted resilience projects includes ₱650 million for the DPWH to retrofit and strengthen the San Juanico Bridge in Region VIII, ₱385.1 million for the DND-OCD’s NDRRMC Integrated Logistics Hub at Lumbia Airport, and ₱44.8 million for DSWD command center repairs in Clark and rescue vehicle procurement.

Following these releases, the NDRRMP holds an available balance of ₱9.5 billion. When combined with the untouched DRRAP at ₱15.3 billion and the total PSF at ₱1.3 billion, the government retains ₱26.1 billion to address disaster-related and climate-mitigation requirements for the remaining four months of the year.

As one of the most well-known celebrity couples of their generation, Gabbi Garcia and Khalil Ramos have kept it real both on and off camera.

“Of course, proud na proud ako. And si Khalil naman, I have no doubts about that guy. If other people tell me, like, ‘Uy, ang galing ni Khalil, ang bait niya. He is the best leading man,’ I have nothing but praise for him,” Gabbi said.

For Gabbi, it is especially fulfilling to see Khalil receive the kind of praise she has long believed he deserves.
“Super proud ako sa kanya and walang question dun. I'm happy that I'm able to share him with other people kasi he really is a good guy,” Gabbi added.

Despite working on different projects and alongside both new and longtime co-stars, Gabbi and Khalil always find ways to support and complement each other. One example was when Khalil served as Gabbi’s personal photographer during the media conference for “The Voice Kids.”

articles.title: Butuan City declared under state of calamity due to water crisis
articles.summary: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425…

blocks.text: BUTUAN CITY – This region’s frontier and capital city Butuan has been declared under a state of calamity due to water shortage for almost three weeks now. Because of the severe water problem, 91,425 families, or more than of its 269,000 residents, have been experiencing almost no-water service as water availability have continued to decline, particularly in the city's 11 most-populated barangays. Accordingly, the water shortage was linked to the prevailing dry spell in this capital city of Caraga region, which has experience a significant rainfall deficit. Butuan City Mayor Lawrence Lemuel “Law” H. Fortun ordered the implementation of water rationing in most affected areas, but these interventions have remainedinsufficient as the shortage continued. Fortun now centered the use of 30-percentQuick Response Fund to the most affected barangays. The state of calamity declaration is expected to allow the city government and affected barangays to mobilize additional resources and access Quick Response Funds for emergency measures, including the provision and installation of water tanks, tankers, pumps and filtration systems, as well as other equipment needed for water distribution and rationing. The state of calamity was declared over the weekend, during the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) Third Special Session, the approval of SP Resolution No. 17-444-2026 at the City Hal Conference Room here. “The resolution was approved as the continuing water shortage has significantly affected residents’ access to water across several barangays,” the SP Resolution said. “We are doing our very best to address this problem,” Mayor Fortun said. The water crisis comes as Agusan del Norte and Butuan City, continues to experience a significant rainfall deficit. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) placed the province under “Dry Spell” status as of August 23, 2026.

articles.summary: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning…

blocks.text: Rene Baterbonia's image and story have continued to appear across social media and music-streaming platforms, months after the Ateneo de Manila University basketball player died in a drowning incident.
Among those circulating online are songs dedicated to Rene, with some using AI-generated music and others appearing to be AI covers or altered versions of existing songs.
One example is “Kalapastanganan,” credited to fitterkarma, which has been re-presented as AI covers of various genres and styles.
Other Rene-related releases include “Baon ang Pangarap,” credited to Andrei AI Music and “Tribute for Rene Baterbonia” by Nihvan.
There are also other music uploads carrying Rene’s name or referencing his death, showing how his story has continued to circulate beyond social media and into streaming services.
There are also AI-generated videos featuring Baterbonia in different scenarios, from still playing basketball to rising out of waters to begging for social media interactions.

These digitally created clips have added another form of online remembrance surrounding the late athlete, with his likeness being used to depict moments and activities that did not necessarily occur in real life.

The growing collection of AI-generated and AI-assisted content has effectively created a digital archive of sorts around Rene, combining original tribute material, covers, edited imagery and fabricated video scenes.
Meanwhile, Rene’s mother continues to ask supporters to keep the focus on prayer and the family’s ongoing pursuit of justice.
In a Facebook post on September 5, Rovelyn asked supporters not to hold a large celebration or bring material offerings to her son’s grave for his 90th or 100th day commemoration.
“Gusto ko lang ng simpleng pagdasal,” she wrote, explaining that she wants to prioritize the case involving her son.
Rovelyn also said that people who wish to help the family financially may send voluntary assistance directly to her instead of bringing food, decorations or other material gifts.

She included her e-wallet details in the post and asked donors to provide screenshots of their transactions for verification. The request follows previous statements from Rovelyn concerning financial assistance and the use of her son's name.
Rovelyn has consistently maintained that justice remains her primary concern.
“Hustisya po ang hiling ko di po PERA,” she previously said, while expressing gratitude to those who continued to support the family.
Meanwhile, Ateneo de Manila University said in August that it remained in communication with the Baterbonia family and was willing to meet with them to provide answers and support.

articles.title: Breakneck finish looms as ICTSI Summit Point unfolds on Tuesday
articles.summary: LIPA CITY, Batangas – Justin Quiban is back, Angelo Que is hungry for another title, and a host of power hitters and young guns are primed to make their move. With the Philippine Golf Tour’s first…

blocks.text: LIPA CITY, Batangas – Justin Quiban is back, Angelo Que is hungry for another title, and a host of power hitters and young guns are primed to make their move.

With the Philippine Golf Tour’s first four legs producing three one-stroke finishes, another breakneck battle looms as the ICTSI Summit Point Championship gets going Tuesday, Sept. 8, at the Summit Point Golf and Country Club here.

Quiban returns to the local circuit after a stint overseas, where he continued to sharpen his game following his stirring come-from-behind victory at Lakewood in the season’s opening leg. Que, meanwhile, is out to build on his clutch performance at Caliraya Springs, where he scrambled his way to a dramatic last-hole escape over fellow veteran Tony Lascuña.

And with Lloyd Go, winner of the last two legs at Pinewoods and Pradera Verde, opting to compete abroad in pursuit of added experience and game enhancement, the title chase has been thrown even wider open.
The stage is therefore set for another highly charged four-day shootout, with established stars, emerging talents and a growing band of contenders all capable of seizing the slightest opening.
Summit Point should provide the perfect test.

The course has held its own despite the recent mix of sun and rain, and while its well-maintained layout may look inviting, it can quickly turn daunting when approached without discipline. Softer fairways could encourage the Tour’s big hitters to attack more aggressively, but knowing when to unleash the power – and when to throttle back – could prove just as important.
The course rewards boldness, but it also exacts a price for even the slightest lapse in judgment.

Keanu Jahns leads the power-hitting charge, arriving with renewed confidence after a respectable finish in a rare Asian Development Tour event last month. The Fil-German, a four-time PGT leg winner who capped last season with the Match Play Championship, has been knocking on the door again and feels it is time to reclaim the spotlight.

Jahns opened the season with a third-place finish at Lakewood, followed it with sixth at Caliraya Springs, stumbled to joint 28th at Pinewoods, then bounced back with another third-place showing at Pradera Verde. He now hopes to turn that roller-coaster run into another victory at Summit Point.

Sean Ramos likewise enters the week with title aspirations. The young standout, who broke through for his first PGT victory in 2024, has spent the last two months competing overseas, further honing a game that increasingly looks ready for another championship run in the P2.5 million event organized by Pilipinas Golf Tournaments, Inc.
He is only one of a talented crop of young players determined to break through.

Carl Corpus has another PGT title firmly in his sights after claiming the Valley Golf leg last year. With the Asian Games looming later this month, Corpus is also using the event as an important competitive tune-up, seeking to find his rhythm early and build the form and confidence needed for the daunting Asiad challenge.

Aidric Chan brings a similar sense of purpose. The former national amateur standout has already secured his first professional victory on the ADT and is now chasing his maiden PGT triumph. Jeffren Lumbo and Russell Bautista are likewise expected to figure prominently in the mix.
But while the young guns bring hunger and momentum, Summit Point’s demanding conditions could tilt the balance toward experience.

That makes the presence of multi-titled campaigners Guido van der Valk, Rupert Zaragosa, Reymon Zaragosa, Jhonnel Ababa, Zanieboy Gialon, Michael Bibat, Jay Bayron and Lascuña all the more significant. Each knows how quickly a tournament can turn and, more importantly, when to press and when to protect a score.
The foreign contingent is equally determined to make its mark.

Korean Taewon Ha, who narrowly missed out at Lakewood, headlines the overseas challenge and returns with another opportunity to break through. Fellow Koreans Kim Tae Soo and Jisung Cheon, as well as Lee Song, are also in the hunt, alongside Japan’s Kashihara Hirotaka, Sena Shiraishi and Nagata Masaki.
With Go absent and no shortage of players carrying either momentum, unfinished business or a larger goal into the week, the Summit Point championship promises another wide-open affair.
The numbers already point to a tight battle. The course could make it even tighter.
And if the first four legs are any indication, expect the championship to be decided by the finest of margins.

articles.summary: Alex Eala will have plenty of time to rest for her next competition following her third-round finish at the US Open in New York over the weekend. The 21-year-old Eala is listed to compete in the…

blocks.text: Alex Eala will have plenty of time to rest for her next competition following her third-round finish at the US Open in New York over the weekend. The 21-year-old Eala is listed to compete in the Singapore Open, a WTA 500 event scheduled on Sept. 21 to 27 at the OCBC Arena. It served as the first tournament in the Asian swing. Based on the latest player list, the tournament draws three of the world’s top 10 players in No. 3 Jessica Pegula, No. 5 and French Open champion Mirra Andreeva, as well as No. 10 and two-time Grand Slam finalist Amanda Anisimova. Other players also competing are two-time Grand Slam champion Barbora Krejcikova, Anastasia Potapova, Donna Vejic and fellow Southeast Asian standout Janice Tjen of Indonesia. The tournament also serves as a prelude to Eala’s reported participation in the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, where competition starts on Sept. 27 to Oct. 2. Currently ranked No. 18, Eala hopes to ride on the momentum of her strong run over the past months, that include her historic fourth-round finish at the Wimbledon, winning her breakthrough WTA title at the Mubadala DC Open in Washington, DC, and her third-round finish at the US Open.

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, Sept. 7, accused authorities of committing “child abuse” over their alleged presence near locations where her mother and children were staying, saying her family should not be used, threatened or dragged into any pressure against her. In a statement released by the Office of the Vice President (OVP), Duterte said she was particularly concerned about authorities approaching or going to locations where her family members, including minors, were staying. “Ang paglapit o pagpunta sa lugar kung saan naroroon ang aking ina at mga anak, sa kabila ng pag-amin ng DILG Secretary at ng pulisya na alam nila kung nasaan ako dahil sa kanilang surveillance activities, ay isang seryosong usapin, lalo na kung nadadamay o naaapektuhan ang mga menor de edad (Approaching or going to the place where my mother and children are, despite the admission of the DILG secretary and the police that they know where I am because of their surveillance activities, is a serious matter—especially when minors are affected or dragged into the situation),” Duterte said. “Ang mga bata ay hindi dapat ginagamit, tinatakot, o idinadamay sa panggigipit (Children must never be used, threatened, or dragged into harassment),” she said. “Ito ay child abuse (That is child abuse),” she added. READ: https://mb.com.ph/2026/09/05/i-do-not-feel-safe-vp-sara-fears-for-her-life-childrens-safety-after-arrest-warrant Security concerns Duterte said she had previously approached then-Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr. regarding her security, citing the constitutional line of succession. “Dahil ang aking seguridad ay nakaugnay sa Hukbong Sandatahan ng Pilipinas alinsunod sa constitutional line of succession, minabuti kong ipaalam sa dating Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner ang ilang mahahalagang pakiusap (Because my security is linked to the Armed Forces of the Philippines in accordance with the constitutional line of succession, I deemed it necessary to inform former Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner of several important requests),” Duterte said. “Higit sa lahat, hiniling ko na igalang at protektahan ang aking ina at mga anak, at huwag silang idamay o takutin sa kahit anumang gagawin sa akin (Above all, I asked that my mother and children be respected and protected, and that they not be dragged into or threatened by anything directed at me),” she added. Duterte also lamented that a government that fails to respect and protect children demonstrates a lack of concern for the country’s future. “Mga kababayan, ang isang pamahalaang hindi gumagalang at nagpoprotekta sa mga kabataan ay nagpapakita ng kawalan ng malasakit sa kinabukasan ng ating bayan (Fellow citizens, a government that does not respect and protect children reveals a lack of concern for the future of our nation),” Duterte said. Alleged plans date back to 2024 Duterte also claimed that she had received information as early as 2024 about alleged plans involving her and her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte. “Taong 2024 pa lamang ay umabot na sa akin ang impormasyon ng mga planong gawin ni Marcos (As early as 2024, information about Marcos’ plans had already reached me),” Duterte said. “Matagal na ako sa pampublikong serbisyo at nakahanda ako araw-araw sa posibilidad gawa ng aking trabaho (I have long been in public service, and I am prepared each day for the possibilities that come with my work),” she added. Duterte said the alleged plans included an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for her father and attacks against her. “Kabilang sa mga plano ang magkaroon ng ICC warrant kay dating Pangulong Duterte at ang mga gagawin na pag-atake sa akin (Among the plans were the issuance of an ICC warrant against former President Duterte and attacks directed at me),” she said. Surveillance allegations Duterte’s latest accusation followed her Sept. 5 allegations that the Marcos administration had been conducting surveillance and harassment operations against her and her family. She cited remarks from Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, who said authorities knew her whereabouts the night before an arrest warrant was issued but did not immediately enforce it. Duterte said Remulla’s statement appeared to support documents she claimed her camp had long held regarding alleged surveillance and harassment operations by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and other government agencies. She also questioned why authorities allegedly went to her mother and children if government agencies already knew her whereabouts. “And because you know where I am, an important question you should answer is—why did you still need to go to my mother and children?” she said. She alleged that the purpose was to intimidate her family. “Isa lamang ang malinaw na sagot—upang takutin at sindakin ang aking pamilya (There is only one clear answer—to frighten and intimidate my family),” Duterte said. Duterte also said she did not trust the police and maintained that she could not surrender to authorities because she did not believe the government could guarantee her safety while in custody. She invoked the arrest and transfer of her father to the custody of the ICC, which she characterized as a “kidnapping” by the PNP. Duterte’s allegations come amid continuing political and legal tensions between her camp and the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., including disputes involving law enforcement, her family and legal proceedings. articles.title: Jonvic: Plan to 'dramatize' VP Sara arrest prevented
articles.summary: Police prevented the alleged plot to exploit the service of the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte through what a ranking official described as a planned drama that includes images of…

blocks.text: Police prevented the alleged plot to exploit the service of the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte through what a ranking official described as a planned drama that includes images of her in handcuffs and inside a detention facility. Duterte was issued with an arrest warrant by a Quezon City Regional Trial Court for a case of grave threats and Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the plan was to make it appear that the Vice President was being treated unfairly. “Ang drama nila gusto nila makulong siya, at naka-hand-cuff siya. The high drama na dapat makulong siya agad dito. (Their drama is that they want her behind bars and in handcuffs. The high drama that she should be jailed here (Camp Crame) right away,” said Remulla in a press briefing. “Hindi kami pumayag (We did not agree). We wanted to go according to the rules to the rues of law and to the rules of court and we accorded her the respect that her positions deserve,” she added. The Department of Justice filed charges of grave threats against Duterte in connection with the assassination threat she allegedly said in an online discussion with vloggers—threats directed to President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. On Friday, Sept. 4, the QC RTC Branch 98 issued an arrest warrant against her. The following day, Duterte arrived at the QC RTC to post bail. It was then that Durerte was quoted accusing the PNP of harassment, and remarked that she fear for her life and that she does not trust the court and the police. The truth according to the PNP Both Remulla and the Philippine National Police (PNP), through the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG), denied the allegation of harassment and surveillance. In a press briefing on Monday, Sept. 7, CIDG director Maj. Gen. Robert Alexander Morico narrated what actually happened the moment they received the arrest warrant from the Branch 98 of the QC RTC. He said the CIDG received the arrest warrant at 12:45 p.m. and immediately, a team from the unit’s Women and Children Protection Desk proceeded to Mandaluyong City where the Vice President is holding office to inform her camp of the court’s order. “We have coordinated with the Vice President Security Group because the subject of the warrant of arrest is the second highest official of the land and we know that there are security arrangements for the President and the Vice President,” said Morico. Morico said they have been in constant coordination with Duterte’s security officer in relation to the service of the arrest warrant and her camp, sent a certain Major Nabua to personally coordinate. The initial arrangement According to Morico, there were already negotiations between the CIDG and the Vice President Security Group since the issuance of the arrest warrant on Friday—and part of that coordination was the visit of the certain Major Nabua whom he said, interestingly asked where the Vice President would be detained inside Camp Crame. “I told him that there is still time for the Vice President to post bail because it’s a bailable offense, that we can escort her after all the booking procedures to the QC RTC to post bail,” said Morico. Morico said they were later told that the Vice President did not want to post bail. “But I was informed of the VSPG that she does not want to post bail. She wants to be incarcerated so they asked where is the jail facility,” said Morico. ‘I told the Major Nabua and his commanding officer that I will not commit the Vice President to jail facilities. She will be placed to conference room because we have to afford her the necessary respect due to her office,” he stressed. Of Jollibee and McDo Morico said they could not commit Duterte to any jail facility because they are full of notorious criminals and that the main detention facilities are undergoing renovation. The most that the CIDG could do, according to her, is to accommodate her to the CIDG conference room with some amenities that include a folding bed and the most expensive meal that the police could afford—from Jollibee and Mc Donald. “But we told them that they can bring food,” said Morico. Change of mind According to Morico, he said they waited until 1 a.m. the following day but did not show up. Instead, he said they were informed that the Vice President would go to QC Regional Trial Court instead to post bail. “So I dispatched a team to the house of the Vice President in San Juan to escort her. No need for armed unit because she has her own coming from the VSPG,” said Morico.

articles.title: San Lazaro Hospital reports downward trend in leptospirosis admissions
articles.summary: Leptospirosis admissions at San Lazaro Hospital are on a downward trend, with the daily count dropping to four on Monday, Sept. 7. The hospital recorded its highest daily admission count at 50 on…

blocks.text: Leptospirosis admissions at San Lazaro Hospital are on a downward trend, with the daily count dropping to four on Monday, Sept. 7. The hospital recorded its highest daily admission count at 50 on Aug. 26, after which admissions declined before rising again to 40 on Sept. 3. The number then dropped to 23 on Sept. 5, 13 on Sept. 6, and four on Sept. 7. More patients were also discharged than admitted over the past two days, with 32 patients discharged on Sept. 6 and 34 on Sept. 7. Monitoring continues following the Aug. 17 and 29 flooding in Metro Manila brought by the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” which may have exposed residents to contaminated floodwaters. Leptospirosis is associated with exposure to water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals. San Lazaro Hospital advised the public to avoid wading in floodwaters and to wash with clean water and soap after possible exposure. People are also advised to keep their surroundings clean and free from rodents, drink safe water, and eat well-cooked food. Those exposed to contaminated floodwaters should watch for symptoms such as fever, headache, muscle pain, and jaundice and seek immediate medical attention if they develop them. articles.title: Free Legal Consultation Service Expanding for Japanese Abroad
articles.summary: Tokyo, Sept. 6 (Jiji Press)--Japan's Foreign Ministry is working to expand a support system that allows Japanese nationals and their families abroad who have become victims of crimes to consult local…

blocks.text: Tokyo, Sept. 6 (Jiji Press)--Japan's Foreign Ministry is working to expand a support system that allows Japanese nationals and their families abroad who have become victims of crimes to consult local lawyers free of charge.

The initiative was first introduced in China last year and has since been launched in the Philippines and Thailand. The ministry aims to make the service available in more and more countries, particularly focusing on nations with many incidents and large numbers of consultations.

The system was established in the wake of an incident in which a Japanese boy was stabbed to death in the Chinese city of Shenzhen in September 2024. As the bereaved family faced difficulties navigating legal procedures that differ from those in Japan, the ministry began to consider offering Japanese-language lawyer consultations and launched the program in China in January 2025.

The ministry assumes that the service is available mainly to victims of serious crimes such as murder, bodily injury, assault, domestic violence, nonconsensual sexual intercourse and indecent assault. Those seeking assistance can apply through a Japanese diplomatic mission abroad to receive from lawyers explanations on how to submit victim reports and on investigation and trial procedures, as well as advice on seeking damages and compensation.
“The number of consultations is increasing, and there is demand," a government official said.
Due to budget constraints, however, free consultations are limited to three sessions per case. A list of local lawyers will be provided upon request.

The initiative was rolled out in the Philippines in May this year and in Thailand last month. The launch in the two Southeast Asian countries was prompted by a shooting incident in the Philippines in August 2025 that killed two Japanese nationals and the fact that Thailand recorded the highest number of incidents in 2025 in which government support was provided.
“Criminal cases are especially common in Asia," a senior Foreign Ministry official said.

Crimes and accidents involving Japanese citizens as victims have been prevalent in recent years. In 2025, Japanese nationals received government support in 12,239 cases abroad. Of the total, 5,633 cases were in Asia, with 705 involving crime victims.
“Awareness of the system is still low," a Foreign Ministry official said. "We want victims, including those of domestic violence and sexual assault, to consult Japanese diplomatic missions first."

articles.title: Balisacan: AI can fight corruption, monitor projects, speed up government
articles.summary: The Marcos Jr. administration plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline government processes, monitor infrastructure projects, and help fight corruption as it prepares a governance…

blocks.text: The Marcos Jr. administration plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline government processes, monitor infrastructure projects, and help fight corruption as it prepares a governance framework for the rapidly evolving technology, according to the country ’s chief economist. Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan told reporters last week that AI could be deployed across critical public sectors, including education, health, and infrastructure, to improve government efficiency and accelerate the delivery of public services. Balisacan identified project monitoring as among the most practical applications of AI, particularly in tracking infrastructure development and ensuring projects are completed on time. The DEPDev chief said AI could also be applied to public-private partnership (PPP) projects. He said automating government processes through AI could also strengthen efforts against corruption. The AI governance framework is “more or less finished,” Balisacan said, with its formal release possibly this month, depending on President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s schedule. He said the President could still propose changes to make the framework more workable and flexible as the government seeks to use AI as a tool for development. The framework builds on the National AI Strategy of the Philippines (NAIS-PH), which the government approved in May 2025. The government’s push to integrate AI into its operations forms part of a broader effort to harness the technology to raise productivity and support economic development while preparing Filipino workers and industries for the disruptions it could bring. Balisacan earlier said fears that AI could cause massive job losses in the country’s information technology and business process management (IT-BPM) industry may be overstated, as the sector continues to expand despite the rapid adoption of the technology. Speaking at the Economic Journalists Association of the Philippines (EJAP) Economic Forum last month, Balisacan identified innovation and productivity as major sources of economic growth and stressed the need to upskill the Filipino workforce to adapt to emerging technologies such as AI. The DEPDev chief also pointed to the proposed Pax Silica development in New Clark City as an opportunity to diversify the economy by attracting investments that support industrialization and higher-value activities. The government, however, faces challenges in building the foundations needed to maximize the economic benefits of AI. Manila Bulletin reported earlier the World Bank ’s warning that weak and fragmented data systems could hold back the country’s AI ambitions and recommended the formulation of a cohesive government data strategy identifying the investments needed in data, infrastructure, and people. The proposed strategy could form part of the data pillar of the AI governance framework being developed under the National Innovation Council (NIC), with DEPDev among the lead agencies. Beyond government operations, Balisacan has identified potential AI applications in the energy sector to optimize power grids while promoting greener and more efficient operations. He also sees AI-enabled assistive technologies playing a role in healthcare and social inclusion as the country’s population ages. Balisacan has also stressed the importance of expanding the country’s digital infrastructure through initiatives such as eGovPH, the national fiber backbone, satellite internet, and the Konektadong Pinoy Act. He has likewise emphasized the need for ethical and trustworthy AI use, including adherence to Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)-Civil Service Commission (CSC) guidelines on responsible AI use in government to uphold transparency and accountability.

articles.title: Kumamoto Quake Victims Begin Moving into Temporary Housing
articles.summary: Hikawa, Kumamoto Pref., Sept. 5 (Jiji Press)--Residents of the town of Hikawa in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, whose homes were damaged in a massive earthquake in late July began moving…

blocks.text: Hikawa, Kumamoto Pref., Sept. 5 (Jiji Press)--Residents of the town of Hikawa in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, whose homes were damaged in a massive earthquake in late July began moving into emergency temporary housing Saturday. A total of 20 makeshift housing units were built in the town, which experienced shaking of 7, the highest level on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, in the 7.1-magnitude quake around 4:27 p.m. on July 28. They are the first temporary housing made available in the prefecture after the earthquake. A ceremony to hand over keys to the housing units was held from around 9 a.m. Saturday, with Kumamoto Governor Takashi Kimura and Hikawa Mayor KazuomiFujimoto in attendance. Attendees observed a moment of silence for quake victims. "We will do all we can for reconstruction so that all residents can regain their normal lives as soon as possible," Fujimoto said in an address. Kimura vowed to provide solid support in cooperation with the town. Takahiro Miyagawa, 73, who received the keys on behalf of the new residents, had lived in a relative's house since the quake, which completely destroyed his home. "I'm relieved that I can finally move in," he told reporters. "We'll make a fresh start." The 20 single-story emergency homes made with lightweight steel frames stand on the site of a former town-run housing complex, with 15 of them having two rooms and a kitchen and the other five with three rooms and a kitchen. Evacuees will be able to live in the temporary homes for up to two years in principle. Similar homes are being built in the Kumamoto cities of Uki and Yatsushiro, which also suffered extensive damage from the temblor. According to the Kumamoto prefectural government, fatalities from the earthquake stood at 38 as of 2 p.m. Friday, including two whose deaths were suspected to have been indirectly caused by the disaster. A total of 64,903 residential buildings were damaged, including 1,748 that were completely destroyed. The temblor struck about 10 years after Kumamoto was hit by two powerful earthquakes in April 2016, which also measured up to 7 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale.

articles.title: Antonelli charges from back to win epic Italian GP
articles.summary: MONZA, Italy (AP) — Kimi Antonelli took a big step to becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history with a fightback for the ages at his home grand prix on Sunday, Sept. 6. Antonelli stormed to…

blocks.text: MONZA, Italy (AP) — Kimi Antonelli took a big step to becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history with a fightback for the ages at his home grand prix on Sunday, Sept. 6. Antonelli stormed to victory at the Italian Grand Prix, despite having started 19th on the grid. It took the Mercedes driver fewer than 17 laps to fight his way to the front. The rest of the race was spent tussling with teammate and title rival George Russell for the lead. Antonelli passed him for the final time with three laps remaining, going on to become the first Italian to win at Monza in 60 years. “Oh my God ... It feels like a dream,” Antonelli said on team radio after crossing the line. ‘Unbelievable, unbelievable’ “I did not expect it," Antonelli said later. “Unbelievable, unbelievable. I am so happy, I could not have imagined to be here today but we managed to pull it off and I am really, really happy.” It was the second furthest back anyone has come from to win a grand prix. John Watson won at Long Beach in 1983 despite starting 22nd. “The best (race) is yet to come. But I feel like it was one of the best races I've done so far and one that I will remember forever,” said the 20-year-old Antonelli, who is in his second season in F1. Antonelli’s triumph at least gave the crowd something to cheer about after Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc crashed out of the scuderia’s home race early on. In the other Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton finished sixth. Max Verstappen was a distant third behind the two Mercedes, just ahead of the McLaren duo of defending champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. It was Antonelli’s seventh win of the season — and his fledgling F1 career — and extended his lead in the overall standings to 66 points ahead of Russell. Russell had been hoping to make up some ground on Antonelli in the title race as his teammate took on a hefty grid penalty at Monza after Mercedes opted to swap his car’s power unit. “Kimi is in control of it and he’s deserving to be in control of it,” Russell said about the title race. "For me personally, I’m not even thinking about a fight or a comeback or anything. “He’s performing incredibly well. It’s going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap so I’m just sort of accepting that it is what it is.” Fans in tears Russel started Sunday's grand prix second and got ahead of surprise polesitter Pierre Gasly at the start of the second lap. Moments later the race was red-flagged after Leclerc lost control coming out of Parabolica at the end of Lap 2 and swerved off into the barriers at high speed. He got out of his car and sat down near the track, looking heartbroken. The hordes of passionate, red-clad tifosi around the track looked similarly despondent, with many in tears. By that point Antonelli was already up to 12th and — as he later admitted — starting to believe in victory. When the race resumed, he continued to slice swiftly through the field, picking off the cars one by one until he only had Russell ahead. No yo-yo The Mercedes duo were told off by their team as they yo-yoed for the lead and instructed to build a gap over Verstappen before fighting it out for the victory. Antonelli was brought into the pits under the virtual safety car on lap 29, while Russell stayed out. Antonelli came out in sixth but, with fresh tires, started reeling Russell in for the second time in the race. “To be honest, I thought we were both going to stay out,” Russell said. "I was surprised to see him pitting. "In the end it was a roll of the dice both ways. In the moment, the team wouldn’t have known which strategy was better, made sense to split the car. In the end Kimi had great pace.” Antonelli looked as though he may have blown his chances of a stunning comeback win when he ran through the gravel as he attempted to get past Russell on Lap 49. But such was his pace that he soon closed the gap that had opened up and breezed past the following lap.
